algorithm.title: Panic disorder and agoraphobia evaluation

nodes.text: Diagnose agoraphobia when fear of difficult escape or unavailable help causes avoidance across at least two situation categories.
**Fear centers on scrutiny or embarrassment:** evaluate for social anxiety disorder.
**Recurrent unexpected panic attacks with persistent worry:** assess for comorbid panic disorder.
**Atypical palpitations, stimulant exposure, or thyrotoxic features:** target ECG, substance history, or TSH to the suspected cause.
Offer CBT with graded exposure to avoided situations.
**Persistent impairment despite CBT or comorbid panic disorder:** consider sertraline or venlafaxine.
**Panic prevents essential travel or procedures:** consider a brief course of lorazepam while initiating longer-term treatment.

f120-2023-q085.boardCall: Clustered pleomorphic microcalcifications on screening mammography -> Ductal carcinoma in situ
f120-2023-q085.hinge: Tightly grouped, pleomorphic, linear, or branching microcalcifications on screening mammography are the classic presentation of ductal carcinoma in situ.
f120-2023-q085.trap: Sclerosing adenosis or fat necrosis can cause calcifications, but tightly clustered pleomorphic microcalcifications represent DCIS until proven otherwise.

A.fit: Here: 20 pleomorphic microcalcifications in 1-cm cluster, age 50

B.fit: Not here: presents with lipid vacuoles and coarse rim calcifications after trauma

algorithm.title: Evaluation of mammographic microcalcifications

nodes.text: Grouped pleomorphic or branching microcalcifications suggest ductal carcinoma in situ.
Obtain diagnostic magnification views and stereotactic core biopsy of suspicious calcifications.
**Localized DCIS with feasible clear margins:** perform lumpectomy, typically followed by radiation.
**Diffuse DCIS or inability to achieve clear margins:** consider mastectomy.
**Estrogen receptor-positive DCIS:** discuss endocrine therapy to reduce subsequent breast events.
Arrange surveillance mammography of remaining breast tissue.

f120-2023-q087.hinge: Lactational mastitis is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus and requires oral anti-staphylococcal penicillin (dicloxacillin or cephalexin) while continuing breastfeeding.
f120-2023-q087.trap: Breast binder or weaning is contraindicated because milk stasis exacerbates infection; continuing breastfeeding or pumping is essential.

A.fit: Not here: contraindicated; worsening milk stasis increases risk of breast abscess

B.fit: Here: fever 38.9 C, wedge-shaped erythema, poor latch

C.fit: Not here: presents with shooting nipple pain and shiny scaling, not focal cellulitis

algorithm.title: Management of lactational mastitis

nodes.text: Lactating woman with focal breast pain + wedge-shaped erythema + fever >= 38.3 C: lactational mastitis
Prescribe oral anti-staphylococcal antibiotic: dicloxacillin or cephalexin
**MRSA risk factors or severe allergy:** treat with clindamycin or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
Strongly encourage continued breastfeeding or pumping every 2-3 hours to relieve milk stasis
Apply warm compresses before feeding + cold compresses and analgesics after feeding
**Persistent fever or fluctuant mass after 48-72 hours:** obtain ultrasound to rule out breast abscess

B.fit: Not here: height is at 30th percentile with normal growth tracking

nodes.text: Female adolescent presenting with absence of secondary sexual characteristics
Determine patient chronological age and assess thelarche (breast development)
**Age < 13 years with Tanner stage 1:** normal physiological variant
Reassure patient and family; no additional diagnostic testing indicated at this time

algorithm.title: Diagnostic workup of hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia

nodes.text: Document Whipple triad: hypoglycemic symptoms + blood glucose <= 55 mg/dL + symptom relief with glucose
Obtain critical blood draw during hypoglycemia: glucose + insulin + C-peptide + sulfonylurea screen

Abdominal CT or MRI shows no abnormalities; evaluate for factitious disorder
**Elevated insulin + elevated C-peptide + negative sulfonylurea:** suspect insulinoma (order multiphase CT)
**Elevated insulin + elevated C-peptide + positive sulfonylurea screen:** oral secretagogue ingestion

abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.name: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm
abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.scope: screening recommendations (men 65-75 who smoked), ultrasound imaging, surveillance intervals, elective repair thresholds, rupture
abdominal-aortic-aneurysm.core: Older adult with abdominal aortic dilation may remain asymptomatic until expansion or rupture; sudden abdominal/back pain and hypotension require immediate vascular rescue.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking strongest modifiable risk; older age, male sex, family history, hypertension, atherosclerosis
Women have higher rupture risk at smaller diameters; most aneurysms infrarenal
Existing AAA: **diameter and high BP** predict rupture; cholesterol, A1c do not

rows.label: Clues
items: Incidental pulsatile expansile abdominal mass; localized persistent pain suggests symptomatic aneurysm
Rupture triad incompletely present; transient stability may reflect contained retroperitoneal hemorrhage
Blue toe/distal ischemia may result from mural thrombus embolization
Acute back pain unchanged by movement = **referred pain**; prevertebral calcification on x-ray; not disc disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Medial elastin/collagen degradation → progressive enlargement; greater wall radius increases tension

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Abdominal ultrasound** diagnoses AAA, generally diameter ≥3 cm; no contrast required
★ Stable suspected rupture or preoperative planning → **CT angiography**
Unstable suspected rupture → bedside ultrasound if immediate; no CT transport delaying surgery
Ultrasound detects aneurysm but cannot reliably exclude rupture; follow symptoms/hemodynamics

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Rupture → **urgent vascular repair**, IV access, blood products; avoid delaying for complete workup
Permissive hypotension during transfer/resuscitation until hemorrhage control when clinically feasible
★ Elective repair: **≥5.5 cm men, ≥5.0 cm women**, symptoms; **not if short life expectancy** (metastatic cancer)
Rapid growth ≥0.5 cm/6 months → repair consideration; endovascular versus open based on anatomy/fitness
Smaller asymptomatic lesions → ultrasound surveillance below; refer vascular surgery, manage cardiovascular risks

rows.label: Complications
items: Rupture, thrombosis, distal embolization; repair → AKI, bowel ischemia, endoleak after EVAR
Aortoenteric fistula after prior graft: herald GI bleed → catastrophic hemorrhage; urgent evaluation

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ USPSTF: **one-time ultrasound men 65–75 who ever smoked**; selectively screen never-smoking men
Women never smoked/no family history → no screening; women smokers/family history → USPSTF evidence insufficient
Smoking cessation, BP control, statin for atherosclerotic disease; lifelong imaging follow-up after EVAR

rows.label: Mimics
items: Renal colic: flank-to-groin pain, hematuria; shock atypical
Aortic dissection: abrupt chest/back pain, possible pulse deficits or branch ischemia

amenorrhea.name: Amenorrhea
amenorrhea.scope: Primary amenorrhea (Turner syndrome, Mullerian agenesis, AIS), secondary amenorrhea (pregnancy, functional hypothalamic, hyperprolactinemia, thyroid, premature ovarian insufficiency, Asherman), diagnostic algorithm
amenorrhea.core: Absent menses requires pregnancy exclusion, then assessment of anatomy, estrogen status, thyroid function, prolactin, and the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Weight loss, intense exercise, psychosocial stress; pituitary disease, dopamine-blocking drugs, thyroid dysfunction
Uterine instrumentation, chemotherapy, autoimmune disease; congenital reproductive tract or chromosomal abnormalities

rows.label: Clues
items: Primary: no menarche by 15; absent breast development by 13 also warrants evaluation
Secondary: ≥3 months absent previously regular cycles, or ≥6 months previously irregular
Galactorrhea/headache, visual symptoms, hot flashes, hirsutism, cyclic pelvic pain guide localization
Galactorrhea, hypothyroid signs → TSH first (TRH raises prolactin); unexplained prolactin → pituitary MRI

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Amenorrhea results from axis suppression, ovarian failure, chronic anovulation, or absent/obstructed outflow
Functional: energy deficit disrupts pulsatile GnRH → irregular, low gonadotropins, low estrogen

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **hCG first**, even if unlikely or premenarchal (ovulation precedes menarche); ultrasound assesses uterus, ovaries
★ TSH, prolactin, **FSH/estradiol**; low estradiol: high FSH → ovarian failure; low/normal FSH → hypothalamic/pituitary
**Progestin challenge**: bleed → anovulation (estrogen, outflow intact); no bleed → low estrogen/outflow defect, check FSH
POI before 40: ≥4 months irregular/absent cycles with FSH >25 IU/L; repeat if uncertain
Post-instrumentation amenorrhea with otherwise normal endocrine testing → saline sonography/hysteroscopy for adhesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Functional hypothalamic → **restore energy intake**, reduce excessive exercise, address eating disorder/stress
Prolactinoma → cabergoline; thyroid disease → correct thyroid function; Asherman → hysteroscopic adhesiolysis
★ POI → **estrogen replacement plus progestogen if uterus present**, usually until natural menopause age
Chronic anovulation → endometrial protection with cyclic progestogen or combined contraception; treat underlying cause
Hematocolpos → **transvaginal incision, drainage**; imperforate hymen → **cruciate hymenotomy**; ultrasound if anatomy unclear

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → infertility, low bone density; prolonged unopposed estrogen → endometrial hyperplasia
Absent uterus differs from absent ovaries: fertility options depend on anatomy and gonadal function

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, avoid overtraining/uterine injury; intermittent ovulation still requires contraception

rows.label: Mimics
items: Imperforate hymen: cyclic pain, bulging bluish hymen, hematocolpos
PCOS: hyperandrogenism with chronic anovulation, estrogen generally preserved

table.title: Primary amenorrhea: high FSH or absent uterus → karyotype

anaphylaxis.name: Anaphylaxis
anaphylaxis.scope: Anaphylaxis, angioedema, biphasic reactions, epinephrine autoinjector, emergency airway management
anaphylaxis.core: Rapid multisystem reaction after exposure—or isolated hypotension or airway compromise after a known allergen—requires epinephrine immediately.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Foods, insect venom, antibiotics, latex; exercise can amplify food-triggered reactions
Asthma, prior severe reaction, mast-cell disorders; beta-blockers can complicate treatment

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Urticaria/angioedema + wheeze, stridor, hypotension, or severe GI symptoms**
Skin findings may be absent; hoarseness and tongue swelling predict airway danger
Biphasic recurrence after apparent resolution, especially after severe or undertreated episodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mast-cell/basophil mediators → vasodilation, capillary leak, bronchoconstriction; often IgE-mediated
Epinephrine: α1 reverses vasodilation/edema, β2 reverses bronchoconstriction; albuterol alone misses edema and shock

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; never wait for tryptase or laboratory confirmation
Acute and baseline serum tryptase can support uncertain cases; normal results do not exclude anaphylaxis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IM epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg**, adult 0.3–0.5 mg, lateral thigh; repeat every 5–15 minutes
Supine with legs elevated unless respiratory distress; oxygen, early intubation for progressive obstruction
Profound shock or refractory hypotension → titrated IV epinephrine plus **isotonic boluses**; beta-blocker use → glucagon
Albuterol for residual bronchospasm; antihistamines relieve itching only; steroids do not reliably prevent biphasic reactions
★ Monitor until resolved; **longer observation/admission** after hypotension, repeated epinephrine, or severe asthma

rows.label: Complications
items: Asphyxia, distributive shock, arrhythmia, hypoxic brain injury
Undiluted IV epinephrine bolus errors → ischemia and dangerous dysrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prescribe **epinephrine autoinjector**, demonstrate technique, provide written action plan and allergy referral
Extra device for repeat-dose risk; avoidance, medical alert ID; venom immunotherapy after qualifying sting allergy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal episode: bradycardia, pallor, rapid improvement supine
Bradykinin angioedema: no itching/hives; ACE inhibitor or hereditary disease → airway, icatibant/C1 inhibitor

ankle-and-foot-injuries.name: Ankle and foot injuries
ankle-and-foot-injuries.scope: Lateral ankle sprain, Ottawa ankle and foot rules, RICE therapy, functional rehabilitation, Achilles tendon rupture, plantar fasciitis, calcaneal apophysitis
ankle-and-foot-injuries.core: Mechanism, focal tenderness, weight-bearing ability, and tendon function distinguish ankle sprain from fracture and overuse foot disorders.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Inversion while plantarflexed, prior sprain, poor balance → lateral ligament injury
Running/jumping, sudden training increase, tight calves, obesity; fluoroquinolones/steroids increase tendon rupture risk

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Lateral swelling after inversion → **anterior talofibular ligament** injury most likely
Pain above ankle with external rotation/squeeze → syndesmotic sprain; recovery slower
Focal bony pain, deformity, neurovascular changes, or inability to bear weight → fracture evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Ligament overstretch → microtears or disruption; tendon degeneration predisposes rupture
Repeated loading damages soft tissue; tendon degeneration reduces tensile strength

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Ankle pain + **posterior-edge/tip malleolar tenderness** → ankle radiographs
★ Midfoot pain + **navicular or fifth-metatarsal-base tenderness** → foot radiographs
Either region: inability to take four steps immediately and during evaluation also triggers corresponding radiographs
Examine skin, pulses, sensation; persistent focal pain despite normal films → reassess occult fracture

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Sprain: **protection, ice, compression, elevation**, brief analgesia; early protected weight-bearing
Functional brace + range-of-motion, strength, proprioceptive rehabilitation; avoid prolonged routine immobilization
Displaced/open fracture or neurovascular compromise → urgent orthopedics; immobilize and keep non-weight-bearing

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic instability, recurrent sprains, osteochondral talar injury
Missed syndesmotic injury → prolonged disability; immobilization → stiffness, thrombosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Balance training and bracing** after prior sprain; gradual return when strength/function restored
Gradual training progression, supportive footwear, calf flexibility; avoid premature athletic return

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lisfranc injury: plantar ecchymosis, midfoot instability; weight-bearing radiographs
Septic arthritis: fever, marked passive-motion pain; aspirate joint

table.title: Heel disorders
rows: Pop, weak plantarflexion, abnormal Thompson test
First-step morning pain; medial plantar heel
Active child; posterior heel squeeze tenderness

antepartum-bleeding.name: Antepartum bleeding
antepartum-bleeding.scope: Placenta previa, placental abruption, vasa previa, uterine rupture, transabdominal ultrasound before digital exam, Kleihauer-Betke test, emergent cesarean delivery
antepartum-bleeding.core: Bleeding in later pregnancy requires immediate maternal stabilization and fetal assessment, followed by placental localization before any digital cervical examination.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Previa: prior cesarean, multiparity; abruption: hypertension, cocaine, trauma, prior abruption
Vasa previa: velamentous cord, accessory placental lobe, IVF; rupture: uterine scar, obstructed labor

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Shock may exceed visible blood loss** with concealed abruption or internal hemorrhage
Assess uterine tone, pain, contractions, fetal tracing, membrane status; bleeding volume alone is unreliable

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Maternal placental bleeding versus fetal vessel hemorrhage; vasa previa can rapidly exsanguinate fetus
Placental separation or uterine disruption compromises oxygen delivery independent of maternal external blood loss

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ CBC, type/crossmatch, coagulation studies including fibrinogen; continuous fetal monitoring if viable
★ **Ultrasound before digital examination**; transabdominal first; transvaginal safely clarifies placenta–cervix relationship
Normal ultrasound does not exclude abruption; suspected rupture is a clinical emergency
Rh-negative bleeding/trauma → Kleihauer–Betke or flow cytometry quantifies fetomaternal hemorrhage for anti-D dosing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ ABCs, two large IVs, blood products when needed; **do not delay delivery for imaging if unstable**
Hemorrhage/fetal compromise → emergency cesarean; rupture → laparotomy, uterine repair or hysterectomy
Stable preterm previa → observation, pelvic rest, corticosteroids when eligible; planned cesarean before labor
Abruption: deliver if significant or compromised; vaginal birth possible when stable and imminent or fetal demise
Unsensitized Rh-negative patient → anti-D immunoglobulin; correct abruption-associated coagulopathy

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhagic shock, DIC, AKI, hysterectomy; fetal hypoxia, death, prematurity
Previa plus cesarean scar increases placenta accreta spectrum risk and operative hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP, avoid cocaine/tobacco; prenatal placental/cord localization and planned high-risk delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bloody show: small mucus-streaked bleeding with cervical change
Cervical lesion: contact bleeding, visible source on speculum examination

table.title: Critical distinctions
rows: Bleeding after rupture; sudden fetal bradycardia
Scarred uterus; sudden pain, lost station, fetal bradycardia

antepartum-bleeding.evidence: Not checked online; established obstetric hemorrhage teaching.

antiarrhythmics.name: Antiarrhythmic agents
antiarrhythmics.scope: Class I (sodium channel blockers), Class II (beta-blockers), Class III (amiodarone, sotalol), Class IV (calcium channel blockers), adenosine, adverse effects, toxicity
antiarrhythmics.core: Drug classes control cardiac rate/rhythm; select by stability, ventricular function, and risk of proarrhythmia.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ Regular narrow-complex SVT after vagal maneuvers → rapid IV **adenosine**
Preexcited AF → procainamide or cardioversion; never AV-nodal blockers
AF rate → metoprolol/diltiazem; AF rhythm → selected IC/III; VT → amiodarone/lidocaine

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Adenosine transiently blocks AV-node conduction; does not terminate AF/flutter

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ Amiodarone: **pulmonary fibrosis**, hypo/hyperthyroidism, hepatitis, photosensitivity, corneal deposits
Adenosine: flushing, chest pressure, brief asystole; avoid active bronchospasm

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ **Flecainide/propafenone** after MI or with significant structural heart disease
Verapamil/diltiazem in HFrEF; beta-blockers during cardiogenic shock or severe decompensation

rows.label: Interactions
items: Amiodarone increases warfarin and digoxin exposure; reduce doses and monitor
Beta-blocker + nondihydropyridine CCB → AV block; caffeine antagonizes adenosine

rows.label: Monitor
items: ECG, electrolytes, renal function; correct low K/Mg before QT-prolonging drugs
Amiodarone: baseline/periodic TSH, LFTs; baseline chest x-ray, evaluate new pulmonary symptoms

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Unstable tachycardia with pulse → **synchronized cardioversion**; pulseless VT/VF → defibrillation
Torsades → IV magnesium; recurrent pause-dependent episodes may need pacing

table.title: Classes
rows: QT/torsades; respectively cinchonism, lupus, anticholinergic effects

anticoagulants.name: Anticoagulants
anticoagulants.scope: Warfarin (CYP interactions, INR monitoring, reversal with vitamin K and PCC), heparin and LMWH (protamine reversal, HIT), direct oral anticoagulants (apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, reversal agents)
anticoagulants.core: Anticoagulants prevent clot extension and embolization; drug choice depends on indication, renal function, pregnancy, and bleeding risk.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ **DOACs**: most nonvalvular AF and VTE; warfarin: mechanical valves, rheumatic mitral stenosis
LMWH: pregnancy; UFH: rapid reversibility or severe renal impairment

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Warfarin blocks vitamin K recycling → ↓II, VII, IX, X and proteins C/S
UFH/LMWH enhance antithrombin; UFH inhibits IIa/Xa, LMWH predominantly Xa
Apixaban/rivaroxaban directly inhibit Xa; dabigatran directly inhibits thrombin

rows.label: Adverse
items: Bleeding with all; warfarin → early skin necrosis, fetal injury
★ **HIT**: platelet fall >50%, usually days 5–10; thrombosis more characteristic than bleeding
High INR + bowel obstruction, hemoglobin drop → **intramural small-bowel hematoma**

rows.label: Avoid
items: Suspected HIT → stop every heparin source; start argatroban or another nonheparin anticoagulant
Warfarin initiation during acute HIT; DOACs for mechanical valves or high-risk antiphospholipid syndrome

rows.label: Interactions
items: Warfarin ↑: amiodarone, TMP-SMX/metronidazole, **fluoroquinolones**; ↓: rifampin, vitamin K-rich diet
DOAC exposure altered by strong P-glycoprotein/CYP3A modifiers; NSAIDs/antiplatelets increase bleeding

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Warfarin **INR**, usually 2–3; UFH aPTT/anti-Xa; LMWH/DOACs: renal function, CBC
No routine INR titration for DOACs; LMWH anti-Xa only selected situations

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Acute VTE warfarin → overlap parenteral anticoagulant ≥5 days and until therapeutic INR
Historical Xa antidote andexanet: US sales ended December 2025; use local PCC-based reversal protocols

appendicitis.name: Appendicitis
appendicitis.scope: Acute appendicitis, clinical presentation, pediatric and pregnancy considerations, imaging (ultrasound, CT), surgical management
appendicitis.core: Periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, followed by anorexia and nausea, suggests appendiceal inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adolescents/young adults; luminal obstruction by lymphoid hyperplasia or fecalith
Older adults may have obstructing neoplasm; immunosuppression can blunt findings

rows.label: Clues
items: McBurney tenderness, guarding, fever; Rovsing, psoas, or obturator signs depend on position
★ **Diffuse peritonitis, toxicity, hypotension** → perforation/sepsis until proven otherwise
Young children: nonspecific symptoms and rapid progression; pregnancy: displaced appendix, less reliable examination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Luminal obstruction → distention, venous congestion, bacterial invasion → ischemia/perforation
Visceral midgut pain precedes focal parietal peritoneal irritation

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC, urinalysis, **pregnancy test** in reproductive-age patients; pyuria does not exclude appendicitis
★ Stable nonpregnant adult → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast** when diagnosis uncertain
★ Child/pregnancy → **ultrasound first**; nondiagnostic → MRI without gadolinium, or CT in nonpregnant child
Noncompressible enlarged appendix >6 mm with periappendiceal inflammation supports diagnosis
Clear peritonitis → surgical evaluation; do not delay necessary operation for repeated imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ NPO, **IV fluids, IV opioids, ceftriaxone + metronidazole**, surgical consultation; opioids do not obscure exam
Laparoscopic appendectomy definitive; do not withhold necessary surgery during pregnancy
Selected uncomplicated cases → antibiotics after shared decision; recurrence/failure higher, especially with appendicolith
Localized abscess/phlegmon in stable patient → antibiotics ± image-guided drainage; follow-up based on age/risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Perforation, abscess, peritonitis, sepsis, ileus
Postoperative wound infection, intra-abdominal collection, adhesional obstruction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG, adnexal findings
Ovarian torsion: sudden unilateral pelvic pain; gastroenteritis: diarrhea prominent before diffuse cramping
Mesenteric adenitis: viral prodrome, normal appendix on imaging

appendicitis.evidence: Not checked online; established general-surgery evaluation and treatment principles.

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.scope: Diagnosis, stepwise therapy, acute exacerbation, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction
asthma.core: Variable episodes of wheeze, cough, dyspnea, and chest tightness from reversible expiratory airflow limitation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: **Family history of asthma/atopy**: strongest childhood risk; allergens, viral infections, smoke, occupational sensitizers
Exercise/cold air, aspirin-sensitive disease, nonselective beta-blockers; assess workplace symptom pattern

rows.label: Clues
items: Nocturnal/early-morning symptoms; normal examination between attacks
★ **Silent chest, exhaustion, altered mentation, rising PaCO2** → impending respiratory failure
Acute attack: low peak flow, accessory-muscle use, difficulty speaking
Cough-variant: isolated chronic cough, worse with cold/exercise; normal examination and radiograph

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergen cross-links IgE on **mast cells** → histamine, leukotrienes → bronchoconstriction
Airway inflammation, smooth-muscle constriction, mucus → variable obstruction and hyperresponsiveness
Persistent uncontrolled inflammation → remodeling with incompletely reversible airflow limitation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Spirometry**: obstruction with bronchodilator FEV1 increase >12% and >200 mL in adults
Normal spirometry with suspicion → repeat during symptoms or methacholine challenge
Exercise challenge: postexercise FEV1 fall >10%; assess baseline control before isolated exercise diagnosis
PFT pattern: ↓FEV1, normal/↓FVC, normal/↑TLC from air trapping

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **repeated inhaled albuterol + ipratropium**, oxygen, early systemic glucocorticoids
Severe poor response → IV magnesium; deterioration → intubation; avoid sedatives and routine antibiotics
Exercise symptoms → preexercise albuterol or prescribed ICS-formoterol; persistent symptoms → improve controller
Check technique/adherence before stepping up; uncontrolled despite high-dose ICS-LABA → phenotype-directed biologic referral
Discharge: **PEF ≥70–80% predicted** (less wheeze is unreliable) + 5–7 day **oral prednisone** prevents relapse

rows.label: Complications
items: Status asthmaticus, pneumothorax, respiratory arrest
ICS → thrush/dysphonia; systemic steroids → osteoporosis, hyperglycemia, adrenal suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Written action plan, trigger reduction, smoking cessation, spacer; rinse mouth after ICS
★ GINA: **no SABA-only treatment**, no LABA monotherapy; ICS with every reliever use
Older exam questions (NAEPP) may expect: symptoms ≤2 days/week, awakenings ≤2/month → **SABA alone**; more → daily ICS

rows.label: Mimics
items: Inducible laryngeal obstruction: inspiratory stridor, inspiratory flow-loop flattening
COPD: persistent obstruction, smoking history
HF: edema, elevated JVP, cardiac findings
Deconditioning: obese/sedentary, exertional dyspnea; normal PFTs, no bronchodilator response

attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder.name: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder.scope: Diagnostic criteria across two settings, behavioral rating scales from parents and teachers, behavioral therapy, stimulant pharmacotherapy
attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder.core: Persistent developmentally inappropriate inattention and/or hyperactivity–impulsivity causing functional impairment across settings, with childhood onset.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Strong genetic contribution, prematurity, prenatal tobacco/alcohol exposure; symptoms may persist into adulthood
Learning disorders, anxiety, oppositional behavior, sleep problems and substance use commonly coexist

rows.label: Clues
items: Inattention: lost items, distraction, disorganization; hyperactivity: fidgeting, leaving seat, excessive talking
Impulsivity: interrupting, difficulty waiting; presentations can be inattentive, hyperactive–impulsive, or combined
Academic difficulty alone insufficient; assess family, peer, driving, and workplace function

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Altered dopamine/norepinephrine executive-control signaling; inconsistent performance does not imply deliberate behavior

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **≥6 symptoms per domain**, or ≥5 if age ≥17; duration ≥6 months
★ Several symptoms **before age 12**, present in ≥2 settings, with impairment; exclude better explanations
Parent and teacher DSM-based rating scales, such as Vanderbilt; interview child and evaluate comorbidities
Check vision/hearing, sleep, learning needs; no routine EEG, neuroimaging, or laboratory diagnostic test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Ages 4–5: **parent-training behavioral management** first; methylphenidate for persistent moderate/severe impairment
★ Age ≥6: **methylphenidate or amphetamine** plus behavioral/classroom intervention and educational supports
Atomoxetine, extended-release guanfacine/clonidine when stimulants unsuitable, ineffective, or diversion concerning
Before prescribing: personal/family cardiac history, BP/HR, height/weight; ECG only if cardiac concern
Titrate to function and adverse effects; monitor appetite, sleep, growth, BP, misuse; reassess across settings

rows.label: Complications
items: Injury, academic failure, relationship problems; untreated impairment increases later substance-use risk
Stimulants → appetite suppression, insomnia, tachycardia; atomoxetine → suicidality warning, rare liver injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Routines, sleep, positive reinforcement, school accommodations; secure medication against diversion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Absence seizures: brief stereotyped unresponsiveness with abrupt recovery
Anxiety: attention disrupted by worry
Sleep apnea: snoring, poor sleep, daytime behavioral dysfunction

benign-breast-conditions.name: Benign breast conditions
benign-breast-conditions.scope: Fibroadenoma, fibrocystic changes, intraductal papilloma, breast cyst, fat necrosis, galactocele, breast abscess
benign-breast-conditions.core: Breast symptoms require age-directed imaging and clinical–radiologic concordance; a benign-appearing examination alone cannot exclude malignancy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive hormonal cycling; milk stasis; breast trauma or prior surgery
Smoking predisposes to recurrent subareolar abscess
**Cracked, excoriated nipples** → main portal of entry for lactational mastitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Galactocele: cystic lactational/postlactational mass, no inflammation, varies with feeds; fat–fluid level on imaging
Mastitis: focal tender erythema, fever, no fluctuance; abscess adds **fluctuance**; often Staphylococcus aureus
★ Spontaneous unilateral **bloody single-duct discharge** → usually **papilloma**; exclude malignancy, persistent → surgical evaluation
Nonbloody discharge only on expression, normal exam → **physiologic**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hormone-responsive stromal/glandular tissue produces cyclic changes; duct obstruction causes retained secretions
Adipose injury causes inflammatory necrosis and calcification that can resemble cancer

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Palpable mass **<30 years → ultrasound**; ≥30 → diagnostic mammography with targeted ultrasound
Suspicious solid lesion or imaging–exam discordance → **core needle biopsy**
Simple cyst: anechoic, thin-walled, posterior enhancement; no solid component
Nonlactational abscess or persistent inflammation after antibiotics → exclude underlying carcinoma
Cyclic bilateral nodularity, no dominant mass → **reexamine after menses**, before imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Painful simple cyst → aspiration; nonbloody fluid + full collapse → benign; bloody fluid/residual mass → **biopsy**
Fibroadenoma → observe when concordant; excise if rapidly enlarging, large or symptomatic
Breast pain, no mass, young, normal exam → **reassurance**; fibrocystic pain → supportive bra, topical/oral NSAID
★ Mastitis → **dicloxacillin/cephalexin**, keep breastfeeding/pumping; abscess → add needle/incision drainage; MRSA → clindamycin
Tender lactating lump, no erythema/fever → **warm compresses**, keep nursing; persistent galactocele → aspiration

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent periductal abscess → fistula; incomplete drainage → persistent infection
Proliferative lesions with atypia increase future cancer risk; simple cysts do not

rows.label: Prevention
items: Effective breast emptying during lactation; smoking cessation for recurrent periductal disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cancer: irregular fixed mass, retraction or suspicious nodes
Phyllodes: rapidly enlarging fibroepithelial mass requiring excision

table.title: Common benign findings
rows: Early postpartum; bilateral tense tender breasts, low fever

benign-breast-conditions.evidence: Not checked online; established breast diagnostic principles.

benign-skin-growths.name: Benign skin growths
benign-skin-growths.scope: Seborrheic keratosis, dermatofibroma, acrochordon, lipoma, epidermoid cyst
benign-skin-growths.core: Slow-growing, stable superficial lesions usually need reassurance; morphology guides recognition, while atypical change requires tissue diagnosis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Aging → keratoses; friction, obesity, insulin resistance → skin tags
Minor trauma may precede dermatofibroma; blocked follicular openings favor epidermoid cysts
Lipomas often sporadic or familial; multiple lesions do not automatically imply malignancy

rows.label: Clues
items: Most lesions asymptomatic; irritation, snagging, cosmetic concern may prompt consultation
★ **Rapid growth, ulceration, spontaneous bleeding**, fixation, or new irregular pigment → reassess diagnosis
Deep, painful, enlarging soft-tissue mass, especially >5 cm → evaluate for sarcoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Benign keratinocyte, fibrous, adipose, or follicular proliferation; no inherent need for oncologic excision
Ruptured keratin cyst → sterile inflammation; erythema alone does not prove bacterial infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical lesions → **clinical examination**; compare with surrounding skin and prior photographs
Uncertain pigmented lesion → dermoscopy and biopsy; do not destroy before excluding melanoma
Suspicious deep mass → MRI and specialist-directed biopsy; ultrasound can establish superficial cystic character

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Reassurance** for confidently benign, untroublesome lesions; treatment chosen for symptoms or cosmetic goals
Irritated keratosis/tag → cryotherapy, snip, or shave removal; dermatofibroma usually observed
Symptomatic lipoma → excision; large/deep or suspicious masses need evaluation before office removal
★ Epidermoid cyst → **complete capsule excision** after inflammation subsides; fluctuant abscess → incision/drainage

rows.label: Complications
items: Local irritation, secondary infection, cyst rupture; removal → bleeding, scar, recurrence
Premature reassurance of atypical growth can delay cancer diagnosis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Melanoma: evolving asymmetric pigmentation, irregular border, color variation
Squamous cell carcinoma: indurated, scaly or ulcerated enlarging lesion
Liposarcoma: deep progressive mass rather than small soft mobile nodule

table.title: Morphologic recognition
rows: Firm papule; dimples with lateral compression

benign-skin-growths.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatologic morphology and evaluation principles.

bite-wounds.name: Bite wounds
bite-wounds.scope: Cat bites (Pasteurella multocida), dog bites, human bites (Eikenella corrodens), wound irrigation, closure vs secondary intention, amoxicillin-clavulanate, rabies and tetanus prophylaxis
bite-wounds.core: Animal or human bites combine tissue damage with polymicrobial inoculation; hand injuries and deep punctures carry disproportionate infection risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cat punctures, delayed presentation, diabetes, immunosuppression, asplenia, wounds near joints
Clenched-fist injury over MCP joint → occult human bite with possible tendon penetration

rows.label: Clues
items: Rapid pain, erythema, swelling, drainage; infection may appear within hours after a cat bite
★ Pain with passive movement, restricted motion, systemic toxicity → **deep-space infection**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mixed aerobes/anaerobes introduced below skin; narrow punctures trap organisms
Crush injury and devitalized tissue impair clearance; tendon sheaths permit proximal spread

rows.label: Dx
items: Neurovascular/tendon examination; assess joint penetration and retained foreign material
Radiograph for hand fight bite, suspected tooth fragment, bone injury, or osteomyelitis
Culture infected drainage; no routine culture of an uninfected fresh wound

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Copious irrigation + debridement**; hand elevation, assess need for surgical exploration
★ Human/cat/hand bite prophylaxis or infection → **amoxicillin-clavulanate**; severe → IV ampicillin-sulbactam
Prophylaxis usually 3–5 days; established infection needs longer, guided by depth and response
★ Hand or human bites, punctures, infected wounds → **leave open**; clean facial lacerations → primary closure
Rabies-risk exposure: unvaccinated → wound HRIG + vaccine days 0, 3, 7, 14; immunocompromised add 28

rows.label: Complications
items: Tenosynovitis, septic arthritis, osteomyelitis, bacteremia; asplenia → fulminant Capnocytophaga sepsis
Rabies almost universally fatal after symptoms begin

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Dirty wound: **tetanus booster if ≥5 years**; unknown/incomplete series → vaccine + TIG
Prior rabies vaccination → vaccine days 0, 3; no HRIG; public health assesses animal risk
Healthy dog/cat/ferret available → 10-day observation coordinated with public health; animal-handling education

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonbite cellulitis: no inoculation history or puncture
Crystal arthritis: joint inflammation with crystals, but aspiration still needed if infection possible

table.title: Characteristic pathogens
rows: Eikenella corrodens; mixed oral/skin flora, anaerobes

bone-tumors.name: Bone tumors
bone-tumors.scope: Osteosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, chondrosarcoma, giant cell tumor of bone, osteochondroma, osteoid osteoma, bone metastases, biopsy
bone-tumors.core: Persistent focal bone pain, a growing mass, or a destructive radiographic lesion requires planned evaluation before biopsy or fixation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Osteosarcoma: adolescence, hereditary retinoblastoma (RB1), prior radiation, Paget disease; chondrosarcoma: older adults
Hereditary multiple exostoses predispose to osteochondromas; most adult malignant bone lesions are metastases

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Night/rest pain**, enlarging mass, constitutional symptoms or pathologic fracture → concerning lesion
Osteoid osteoma: nocturnal pain relieved by NSAIDs; small cortical nidus
Osteochondroma: painless metaphyseal exostosis with medullary continuity; new growth after maturity concerning
Known cancer + constant back pain, vertebral point tenderness → **spinal metastasis**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tumor lineage determines osteoid, cartilage or primitive-cell production; aggressive growth destroys cortex
Giant cell tumor: neoplastic stromal cells recruit osteoclast-like giant cells, causing locally aggressive osteolysis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Plain radiographs first**; assess location, margins, periosteal reaction and matrix
Aggressive lesion → MRI entire involved bone/adjacent joint; chest CT for lung metastases
★ **Orthopedic oncology plans biopsy tract**; core biopsy after imaging, before definitive treatment
CBC, ESR/CRP if infection suspected; normal labs do not exclude malignancy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Osteosarcoma → **neoadjuvant chemotherapy + wide resection**, then postoperative chemotherapy
Ewing → systemic chemotherapy plus surgery and/or radiation
Chondrosarcoma → wide surgical excision; conventional tumors relatively chemo/radioresistant
Symptomatic osteoid osteoma → radiofrequency ablation; asymptomatic osteochondroma → observation
Giant cell tumor → curettage/reconstruction; selected unresectable lesions → denosumab

rows.label: Complications
items: Pathologic fracture, neurovascular compromise, pulmonary metastases; limb surgery and chemotherapy morbidity
Mandible metastasis → mental nerve anesthesia (**numb chin**)

rows.label: Mimics
items: Osteomyelitis: infection markers, cultures; may closely resemble Ewing
Bone metastases: older adult, multiple lesions; myeloma: anemia, monoclonal protein
Unicameral bone cyst: child, lucent expansile proximal humerus lesion; pathologic fracture after minor trauma

bone-tumors.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical teaching.

brain-death.name: Brain death
brain-death.scope: Prerequisites (normothermia, normal BP), clinical exam (coma, absent brainstem reflexes), apnea test, ancillary testing (cerebral blood flow studies)
brain-death.core: Permanent loss of all brain function, including brainstem function, constitutes death; a beating heart on ventilation does not negate the diagnosis.

rows.label: Principle
items: Known catastrophic irreversible brain injury; compatible neuroimaging; adequate observation period
No family consent needed; after declaration → stop ventilator, unless organ donation planned

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Prerequisites: **temperature ≥36°C**, adult SBP ≥100 and MAP ≥75 mm Hg
Exclude paralysis/metabolic confounders; sedatives: ≥5 half-lives, longer if impaired clearance
★ Examination: **coma**, no brain-mediated motor response; absent brainstem reflexes (table)

rows.label: Don't
items: Oculocephalic testing with possible cervical injury; use caloric testing after confirming ear integrity
Declare death with any brain-mediated response or spontaneous breath
Use ancillary testing to bypass hypothermia or high CNS-depressant levels

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Spinal reflex movements may persist without contradicting diagnosis
Incomplete examination or unsafe apnea test → radionuclide cerebral perfusion or catheter angiography
After temperature ≤35.5°C, wait ≥24 hours following rewarming to ≥36°C

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Apnea test: no breaths, **PaCO2 ≥60 and ≥20 above baseline**, pH <7.30
Preoxygenate; abort apnea testing for hypotension, hypoxemia or unstable arrhythmia
★ 2023 update: **EEG no longer accepted** as ancillary testing; pediatric requirements differ

breast-neoplasia.name: Breast neoplasia
breast-neoplasia.scope: Ductal carcinoma in situ, invasive ductal and lobular carcinoma, receptor status (ER, PR, HER2), metastatic disease (bone, visceral), surgical management, endocrine and chemotherapy
breast-neoplasia.core: A suspicious breast lesion requires core biopsy, assessment of invasion and ER/PR/HER2 status to guide local and systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, BRCA-related syndromes, close-relative family history (distant relative adds little), prior chest irradiation
**Combined estrogen-progestin therapy**, prolonged estrogen, postmenopausal obesity, alcohol; atypical proliferative lesions

rows.label: Clues
items: Painless hard irregular mass, skin/nipple retraction, unilateral bloody discharge or axillary node
★ Peau d’orange, diffuse erythema and edema → **inflammatory breast cancer**, even without discrete mass
Persistent unilateral eczematous nipple lesion → Paget disease; **full-thickness biopsy**, investigate underlying carcinoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Invasion through basement membrane enables lymphatic/hematogenous metastasis
ER/PR signaling and HER2 amplification create actionable tumor drivers; triple-negative tumors lack these targets

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Diagnostic mammography + targeted ultrasound** → core biopsy of suspicious lesion; pregnancy → **ultrasound first**
Pathology: invasion, grade, **ER/PR/HER2**; assess regional nodes clinically and with targeted imaging
Clinically node-negative invasive disease, including microinvasion ≤1 mm → sentinel node biopsy during definitive surgery
Distant staging scans for advanced disease or suspicious symptoms; not every small asymptomatic cancer
Axillary node adenocarcinoma, normal mammogram → occult breast primary; breast MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early: lumpectomy + radiation or mastectomy; **positive margins → reexcision** before adjuvant therapy
ER-positive → tamoxifen or postmenopausal aromatase inhibitor; chemotherapy based on stage/biology
★ HER2-positive → **trastuzumab-based** treatment, monitor LVEF; triple-negative → chemotherapy ± pembrolizumab if higher-risk
Locally advanced → neoadjuvant treatment, then surgery/radiation; large residual + palpable nodes → **mastectomy + axillary dissection**
Bone metastases → **zoledronate/denosumab**; systemic treatment by receptors, chemotherapy for visceral crisis

rows.label: Complications
items: Metastases to bone (often **mixed lytic–blastic**), lung, liver, brain; surgery/radiation → lymphedema
Tamoxifen → VTE/endometrial cancer; aromatase inhibitors → bone loss; trastuzumab → cardiomyopathy
Prior cancer + severe hypercalcemia, lytic lesions → recurrence; thiazide/calcium supplements cause only mild elevation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Age/risk-based screening, genetic counseling for suggestive pedigree; selected high-risk patients → chemoprevention
BRCA-related very high risk → discuss risk-reducing surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mastitis: lactation-associated tenderness/fever, improves with antibiotics
Fat necrosis: trauma/surgery history; biopsy if discordant imaging

table.title: Histologic distinctions
rows: Bilateral risk marker; discohesive lobular cells
Surveillance/risk reduction if concordant; later cancer usually ductal

breast-neoplasia.evidence: Not checked online; established breast-oncology management principles.

cardiomyopathies.name: Cardiomyopathies
cardiomyopathies.scope: Dilated cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, restrictive cardiomyopathy, stress (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy, viral myocarditis, diagnostic evaluation, management
cardiomyopathies.core: Myocardial disease causes pump failure, impaired filling, dynamic obstruction, or arrhythmias; echocardiography defines the phenotype.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dilated: familial disease, alcohol, anthracyclines, peripartum state, **viral myocarditis**
Hypertrophic: autosomal dominant sarcomeric variants; restrictive: amyloid, hemochromatosis, radiation
Takotsubo: emotional/physical stress; myocarditis: recent viral illness, immune checkpoint inhibitors

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, edema, elevated JVP; **displaced PMI**, S3 → dilated LV; syncope/ventricular arrhythmia signals danger
★ Obstructive HCM murmur **↑Valsalva/standing**, ↓squatting/handgrip; exertional presyncope
Myocarditis: chest discomfort, tachycardia disproportionate to fever, acute heart failure

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Sarcomere dysfunction or myocardial injury → remodeling; infiltration → reduced ventricular compliance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG, troponin, BNP → transthoracic echo**; assess coronary ischemia when suspected
Cardiac MRI: inflammation, scar, infiltrative patterns; iron studies or monoclonal protein testing when relevant
Endomyocardial biopsy: selected fulminant unexplained failure, malignant arrhythmias, suspected giant-cell myocarditis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ HFrEF: **ARNI, evidence-based beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor**; loop diuretic for congestion
Obstructive HCM: nonvasodilating beta-blocker (propranolol, metoprolol); alternative verapamil/diltiazem
Refractory obstruction → myosin inhibitor, disopyramide, or septal reduction; avoid dehydration and vasodilators
Restrictive disease: cautious diuresis, treat cause; Takotsubo: supportive care after excluding ACS
Myocarditis with shock → ICU, circulatory support; no routine antiviral or immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Sudden cardiac death, atrial fibrillation, thromboembolism; advanced failure → transplantation evaluation
★ HCM with cardiac arrest or major sudden-death risk → **ICD** consideration

rows.label: Prevention
items: Screen first-degree relatives in inherited disease; avoid cardiotoxins
Myocarditis: restrict strenuous exercise until clinical recovery and reassessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ischemic cardiomyopathy: obstructive coronary disease explains dysfunction
Constrictive pericarditis: pericardial disease, respiratory ventricular interdependence
Aortic stenosis: murmur softer with standing/Valsalva, unlike obstructive HCM

table.title: Echo phenotype
rows: Enlarged ventricles, diffuse hypokinesia, reduced EF
Transient apical ballooning beyond coronary territory

cardiomyopathies.evidence: HCM checked 2026-10-30: [AHA/ACC 2024](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/05/06/15/12/2024-hypertrophic-cardiomyopathy-gl); other content established teaching.

cat-scratch-disease.name: Cat-scratch disease
cat-scratch-disease.scope: Bartonella henselae, kitten scratch or bite, regional lymphadenopathy, primary inoculation papule, azithromycin therapy, bacillary angiomatosis in immunocompromised
cat-scratch-disease.core: Inoculation papule followed by tender regional lymphadenopathy after a kitten scratch or bite.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Child or young adult with kitten exposure; flea-infested cats more likely infected
Advanced HIV or other immunosuppression → disseminated infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Axillary or cervical nodes appear 1–3 weeks after exposure; low fever, occasional suppuration
★ Bacillary angiomatosis: friable red-purple vascular papules or nodules in immunocompromised hosts

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **Bartonella henselae** causes granulomatous lymphadenitis or endothelial proliferation depending on host immunity

rows.label: Dx
items: Typical lymphadenitis: clinical; atypical disease → Bartonella serology or tissue PCR
Vascular lesions → biopsy showing lobular vascular proliferation, neutrophils and Warthin–Starry-positive bacilli
Persistent fever with hepatosplenomegaly → abdominal imaging for hepatic or splenic microabscesses

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Uncomplicated lymphadenitis often self-limited; **azithromycin** can speed nodal shrinkage
Painful suppurative node → needle aspiration; avoid incision and drainage
★ Bacillary angiomatosis → prolonged doxycycline or erythromycin, generally ≥3 months in HIV

rows.label: Complications
items: Parinaud oculoglandular syndrome, neuroretinitis, hepatosplenic lesions, culture-negative endocarditis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Flea control, avoid rough play with kittens, wash scratches promptly

rows.label: Mimics
items: Kaposi sarcoma: spindle cells, slit-like vessels, HHV-8-positive biopsy
Tularemia: ulceroglandular illness after tick or rabbit exposure

cat-scratch-disease.evidence: Checked CDC Bartonella clinical guidance and NIH HIV opportunistic infection guidance.

child-growth-and-development.name: Child growth and development
child-growth-and-development.scope: Normal growth velocity, weight doubling and tripling milestones, WHO/CDC growth chart interpretation, developmental surveillance, normal toddler behavioral variants (head banging, temper tantrums)
child-growth-and-development.core: Interpret serial growth and developmental progress against age, family pattern, and corrected gestational age; a trajectory matters more than one percentile.

rows.label: Definition
items: Weight doubles by 4–6 months, triples by 12 months, quadruples near 24 months
Length increases about 25 cm during year 1; prepubertal height velocity about 5–6 cm/year
★ **WHO charts before 2 years; CDC charts from 2 years** in US practice

rows.label: Interpret
items: Nutrition failure: weight falls first; endocrine disease: height slows with preserved/increased weight
★ Falling **2 major percentile channels**, well child → **diet diary, calorie counts** before labs
Correct prematurity through about 2 years; track infant head circumference

rows.label: Use when
items: Developmental surveillance every visit; standardized general screens at 9, 18, and 30 months
★ **Regression/missed milestones → early intervention**; language delay → **audiometry** before speech testing
BMI-for-age from 2 years; weight-for-length younger; consider parental heights and pubertal timing

rows.label: Compare
items: Tantrums, picky eating, bedtime separation distress → reassure, routines, calm limits; no sedatives
Head banging at sleep onset or frustration, normal development → self-soothing; assess injuries
Preschool restlessness, good function → no stimulants; overwhelmed parent → **parenting classes**

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **One percentile cannot diagnose disease**; stable tracking + normal exam → reassure
Persistent skill loss needs evaluation; never wait for school failure
Short parents, normal bone age → familial; average parents, delayed puberty → **constitutional delay**

rows.label: Adolescence
items: ★ Moodiness, privacy, family detachment, rule-questioning, late bedtimes, good function → reassure, educate parents
Parental-pressure conflict, occasional experimentation, no impairment → not ODD, substance use disorder
Weight worry, stable percentile, normal BMI, regular menses → normal; not eating disorder

table.title: Normal by age
rows: Holds head up; not yet reaching
Sits unsupported; bangs blocks, self-feeds finger foods
Walks; scribbles; non-walker at 14 months normal
Balances on one foot; copies circle
Same-sex parent preference; involve other parent otherwise

child-growth-and-development.evidence: Checked screening ages 2026-10-30: [AAP surveillance/screening](https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/developmental-surveillance-and-screening-patient-care/); growth facts established pediatric teaching.

clostridioides-difficile-infection.name: Clostridioides difficile infection
clostridioides-difficile-infection.scope: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea, toxic megacolon, pseudomembranous colitis, NAAT vs EIA stool toxin testing, oral fidaxomicin, oral vancomycin, fulminant colitis
clostridioides-difficile-infection.core: Recent antibiotics or healthcare exposure followed by watery diarrhea suggests toxin-mediated colitis; ileus can conceal fulminant disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Clindamycin, fluoroquinolones, cephalosporins, penicillins, even perioperative; older age, hospitalization, immunosuppression
Prior infection and unnecessary acid suppression increase susceptibility or recurrence

rows.label: Clues
items: Onset during or weeks after antibiotics; fecal leukocytes, occasionally blood/mucus; pseudomembranes on endoscopy
Abdominal cramps, fever, leukocytosis; severe disease may cause AKI and hypoalbuminemia
★ **Hypotension, ileus, or megacolon** defines fulminant infection; diarrhea may disappear

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Fecal-oral **ingested spores**; antibiotic disruption of colonic microbiota permits toxigenic bacilli to proliferate
Exotoxins A and B damage colonic epithelium → inflammation and pseudomembranes

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Test **unformed stool** with ≥3 unexplained stools/24 hours; exclude laxative effect
NAAT detects toxigenic genes, not active toxin; positive results can represent colonization
Toxin EIA is less sensitive; multistep GDH/NAAT plus toxin improves clinical specificity
No test of cure; abdominal imaging for distention, toxicity, or suspected perforation

rows.label: Tx
items: Stop inciting antibiotic when possible; replace fluids/electrolytes, avoid antimotility drugs in severe colitis
★ Initial nonfulminant infection: **oral fidaxomicin** preferred; oral vancomycin acceptable, usually 10 days
★ Fulminant: **high-dose oral/NG vancomycin + IV metronidazole**; add rectal vancomycin with ileus
Shock, perforation, worsening organ failure → urgent surgical consultation
Recurrence: fidaxomicin or tapered/pulsed vancomycin; multiple recurrences → screened microbiota-based treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Toxic megacolon, perforation, sepsis, recurrent infection
Severe classification: WBC >15,000/µL or creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL; different from fulminant criteria

rows.label: Prevention
items: Contact precautions, gloves/gown, soap-and-water handwashing, sporicidal surface cleaning
Antibiotic stewardship; no screening/treatment of asymptomatic carriers

rows.label: Mimics
items: Laxative-associated diarrhea: medication timing, no inflammatory syndrome
IBD flare: chronic relapsing course; test for coinfection before escalating immunosuppression
Shigella/Salmonella: dysentery after food or travel exposure, no recent antibiotic

congenital-heart-disease.name: Congenital heart disease
congenital-heart-disease.scope: Cyanotic heart disease (5 Ts: Tetralogy of Fallot, TGA, truncus, tricuspid atresia, TAPVR), acyanotic heart disease (VSD, ASD, PDA, coarctation of aorta), hyperoxia test, prostaglandin E1
congenital-heart-disease.core: Neonatal cyanosis or shock as the ductus closes demands urgent assessment for duct-dependent congenital heart disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Maternal diabetes, congenital rubella, family history; Down syndrome → AV septal defects
Prematurity → PDA; Turner syndrome → coarctation

rows.label: Clues
items: Poor feeding, diaphoresis, tachypnea, hepatomegaly → infant heart failure
VSD: harsh holosystolic lower-left sternal murmur; ASD: **fixed split S2**, pulmonic flow murmur, RV volume overload
PDA: continuous machinery murmur, bounding pulses; coarctation: weak femoral pulses, arm–leg BP gradient
Central cyanosis: blue lips/tongue, warm extremities → **low arterial saturation**; peripheral: cold extremities

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Left-to-right shunts (VSD, ASD, extracardiac PDA) increase pulmonary flow; remodeling can reverse flow → Eisenmenger syndrome
Duct-dependent lesions require pulmonary/systemic flow or mixing through fetal communications
High neonatal PVR limits VSD shunt → murmur appears/louder over weeks as **PVR falls**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Preductal/right-hand and postductal/foot oxygen saturation; **echocardiography** defines anatomy
★ Hyperoxia test: little PaO2 rise with 100% oxygen suggests cardiac shunting; echo preferred
ECG and chest radiograph support diagnosis; normal murmur does not exclude critical disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected duct-dependent lesion → **prostaglandin E1** immediately; monitor for apnea
★ Tet spell (agitation, softer murmur) → knee–chest, oxygen, fluids, morphine; refractory → phenylephrine or propranolol
TGA with inadequate mixing → balloon atrial septostomy, then arterial switch
Large shunts → diuretics, closure; premature PDA → ibuprofen; **obstructed TAPVR → emergency repair**
Coarctation → repair; post-repair paradoxical hypertension → **IV beta-blocker**; Eisenmenger → **do not close shunt**

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, failure to thrive, arrhythmias, infective endocarditis
Right-to-left shunting → brain abscess, paradoxical emboli, secondary erythrocytosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Pulse-ox newborn screening; rubella immunization before pregnancy; maternal glycemic control
Endocarditis prophylaxis for selected unrepaired cyanotic or prosthetic-material lesions during dental procedures

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lung disease: substantial oxygen response, pulmonary findings
PPHN: elevated pulmonary resistance with structurally normal heart

table.title: Five cyanotic lesions
rows: RV obstruction, VSD, overriding aorta, RVH; boot-shaped heart
Parallel circuits; single S2; egg-on-string silhouette
Pulmonary veins drain systemically; obstruction → edema

congenital-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric cardiology teaching.

contact-dermatitis.name: Contact dermatitis
contact-dermatitis.scope: Allergic contact dermatitis (poison ivy/urushiol, nickel, neomycin, type IV hypersensitivity), irritant contact dermatitis, patch testing, topical corticosteroids, allergen avoidance
contact-dermatitis.core: Pruritic eczema confined to an exposure pattern; delayed allergy or direct chemical injury, sometimes spreading beyond contact sites.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Allergens: urushiol, nickel jewelry, fragrances, latex additives, neomycin, occupational chemicals
Irritants: repeated handwashing, detergents, solvents, prolonged wet work; atopic skin increases susceptibility
Repeated surgeries, healthcare work → **latex sensitization**

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Linear vesicles** after outdoor exposure; geometric plaques under jewelry, adhesive, or topical products
Acute: erythema, edema, weeping; chronic: fissuring, scaling, lichenification
Irritant disease often burns or stings; allergic disease usually itches
Extensive blistering, facial swelling, genital involvement → assess severity and secondary infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergic: sensitized T cells mediate **type IV hypersensitivity**; symptoms 24–72 hours after re-exposure
Irritant: direct epidermal barrier damage; no prior sensitization required

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical exposure history and distribution first; review work, hobbies, cosmetics, and new skin products
Persistent or unclear allergic disease → **patch testing**, read after delayed intervals
Skin-prick testing and serum IgE do not diagnose delayed contact allergy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Remove exposure → emollients and **topical corticosteroids**; choose potency by body site
Face, groin, folds: low-potency hydrocortisone; thick extremity plaques: triamcinolone
★ Poison ivy **>20% BSA** or severe face/genital disease → oral prednisone taper **2–3 weeks**
Cool wet compresses for oozing; antibiotics only for bacterial superinfection

rows.label: Complications
items: Excoriation → impetigo; persistent exposure → chronic hand eczema and work disability
Prolonged potent topical steroids → skin atrophy, striae; systemic steroids → hyperglycemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Protective gloves and barrier care; fragrance-free products; avoid the identified allergen
Wash urushiol promptly from skin, clothing, and tools; blister fluid does not spread dermatitis
Hand eczema ± generalized urticaria → latex allergy: **strict avoidance**, including intraoperatively; no desensitization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atopic dermatitis: chronic flexural eczema, personal or family atopy
Tinea: advancing annular scaly border; KOH reveals hyphae
Scabies: nocturnal itch, finger-web burrows, affected close contacts

contact-dermatitis.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatology teaching.

copd.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
copd.scope: Stable COPD, acute exacerbation (AECOPD), oxygen-induced hypercapnia, noninvasive ventilation (NIV/BiPAP), indications for intubation, bronchodilators and glucocorticoids
copd.core: Persistent airflow obstruction after inhalational exposure causes progressive exertional dyspnea and episodic infectious or inflammatory exacerbations.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Tobacco, biomass smoke, occupational dusts; alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with early/basilar emphysema

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic cough/sputum, prolonged expiration, wheeze, hyperinflation
★ **Somnolence, exhaustion, silent chest, worsening acidosis** → impending respiratory failure
Exacerbation: ↑dyspnea, purulent sputum, rhonchi, **no infiltrate** → acute bronchitis, not pneumonia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Small-airway inflammation + alveolar destruction → expiratory collapse, air trapping, impaired diffusion
Excess oxygen worsens CO₂ retention mainly through V/Q mismatch and Haldane effect

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Postbronchodilator FEV₁/FVC <0.70** confirms persistent obstruction in compatible clinical setting
Exacerbation: pulse oximetry; ABG for severe distress/altered mentation; radiograph for pneumonia, edema, pneumothorax
Consider ECG, troponin, BNP, or PE evaluation when symptoms exceed expected exacerbation pattern

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **albuterol + ipratropium**, prednisone for 5 days; titrate oxygen to 88–92%
Antibiotics: purulence + increased dyspnea/sputum volume, or ventilatory support; doxycycline/azithromycin options
★ Hypercapnic acidosis, pH ≤7.35 → **BiPAP** unless aspiration risk, arrest, instability, inability to cooperate
Intubate for failed NIV, severe encephalopathy, refractory hypoxemia, or inability to protect airway
Long-term oxygen if stable PaO₂ ≤55 or saturation ≤88%; selected cor pulmonale/polycythemia with PaO₂ 56–59

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, secondary polycythemia, cachexia
Pneumonia risk with inhaled steroids; ventilation → dynamic hyperinflation, auto-PEEP, barotrauma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Smoking cessation**, influenza/COVID/pneumococcal/RSV vaccination when eligible, pulmonary rehabilitation
Check inhaler technique/adherence; offer alpha-1 antitrypsin testing at least once

rows.label: Mimics
items: Asthma: variable symptoms and reversible obstruction
Heart failure: orthopnea, edema, vascular congestion; bronchiectasis: copious sputum, dilated bronchi

table.title: Stable inhaled treatment
rows: Exacerbations with eosinophilia or concurrent asthma

copd.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [GOLD 2026](https://goldcopd.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/GOLD-REPORT-2026-v1.3-8Dec2025_WMV2.pdf); acute ventilatory care: established teaching.

croup.name: Croup
croup.scope: Parainfluenza virus, barking cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness, steeple sign, Westley score, nebulized epinephrine, dexamethasone
croup.core: A toddler with a viral prodrome develops a barking cough, hoarseness, and inspiratory stridor from subglottic airway narrowing.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Usually 6 months–3 years; parainfluenza most common, other respiratory viruses possible
Autumn/winter exposure, daycare; recurrent or atypical-age episodes suggest structural airway disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Symptoms often worsen at night; low-grade fever, retractions, agitation with respiratory distress
★ **Stridor at rest** marks clinically significant obstruction; cyanosis/lethargy suggests impending failure
Drooling, tripod posture, toxicity, or high fever → reconsider diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Viral laryngotracheal inflammation causes edema within the rigid cricoid ring
Small reductions in pediatric airway radius produce large increases in airflow resistance

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; routine imaging, viral testing, and blood draws unnecessary
AP neck x-ray: steeple-shaped subglottic narrowing, supportive but neither required nor specific
Westley: stridor, retractions, air entry, cyanosis, consciousness; 0–2 mild, 3–7 moderate, ≥8 severe

rows.label: Tx
items: Keep child calm with caregiver; oxygen if hypoxemic; avoid unnecessary upsetting procedures
★ **Dexamethasone once for all severities**; oral route preferred when tolerated
★ Moderate/severe disease → **nebulized epinephrine**; observe ≥2–3 hours after last dose
Persistent resting symptoms, repeated epinephrine, poor intake → admit; exhaustion/hypoxia → expert airway management
No routine antibiotics, bronchodilators, or cough suppressants; humidified air lacks proven benefit

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure, dehydration; rare secondary bacterial tracheitis
Epinephrine effect wears off before steroid benefit; reassess rather than discharge immediately

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hand hygiene, respiratory etiquette, reduced close contact during acute viral illness

rows.label: Mimics
items: Epiglottitis: drooling, dysphagia, muffled voice, tripod posture; secure airway without throat manipulation
Bacterial tracheitis: toxic, high fever, thick secretions, poor epinephrine response
Foreign body: abrupt choking, no preceding viral syndrome

croup.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric emergency teaching.

cystic-fibrosis.name: Cystic fibrosis
cystic-fibrosis.scope: CFTR mutations, meconium ileus, bronchiectasis, pancreatic insufficiency, sweat chloride test
cystic-fibrosis.core: Recurrent sinopulmonary infection plus malabsorption, poor growth or neonatal meconium ileus suggests CFTR dysfunction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive CFTR variants; affected sibling or carrier parents
F508del is common; genotype determines eligibility for specific CFTR modulators

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic productive cough, recurrent pneumonia, nasal polyps, clubbing and bronchiectasis
Greasy stools, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency, failure to thrive despite appetite
Salty skin, dehydration with hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis; male infertility from absent vas deferens
Neonatal abdominal distention with inspissated ileal meconium; later rectal prolapse possible

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Defective apical chloride/bicarbonate transport → dehydrated airway and pancreatic secretions
Sweat ducts fail to reabsorb chloride; pancreatic duct blockage causes exocrine destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Positive newborn immunoreactive trypsinogen screen → **quantitative sweat chloride** confirmation
★ Sweat chloride **≥60 mmol/L** supports CF; 30–59 intermediate → repeat/genetic evaluation
Two CF-causing variants in trans or specialized CFTR-function testing resolve uncertain cases
Fecal elastase assesses pancreatic insufficiency; sputum cultures guide respiratory antibiotics
Consider CF despite negative limited mutation panel when clinical phenotype is compelling

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Daily **airway clearance**, hypertonic saline, dornase alfa; exercise supports mucus clearance
Pulmonary exacerbation → culture-directed antibiotics; Pseudomonas commonly needs antipseudomonal coverage
★ Pancreatic insufficiency → **pancrelipase with meals**, high-calorie nutrition, vitamins A/D/E/K
Eligible genotype → elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor; check liver function and interactions
Advanced respiratory failure → oxygen/ventilatory support and lung transplant assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Pseudomonas colonization, massive hemoptysis, pneumothorax, respiratory failure
CF-related diabetes, biliary liver disease, distal intestinal obstruction, osteoporosis and infertility

rows.label: Prevention
items: Vaccination, nutrition monitoring, salt/fluid replacement during heat or exercise
Infection-control separation between CF patients; family carrier testing and reproductive counseling

rows.label: Mimics
items: Primary ciliary dyskinesia: situs inversus possible; normal pancreatic function/sweat chloride
Immunodeficiency: recurrent infection without CFTR-pattern salt loss
Celiac disease: malabsorption without bronchiectasis

cystic-fibrosis.evidence: Diagnostic threshold checked 2026-10-30: [CF Foundation sweat testing](https://www.cff.org/intro-cf/sweat-test); management established CF teaching.

depressive-disorders.name: Depressive disorders
depressive-disorders.scope: Major depressive disorder criteria, depression in older adults, bereavement vs MDD, pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, suicide risk
depressive-disorders.core: Persistent low mood or loss of pleasure with neurovegetative and cognitive symptoms, causing clinically significant distress or impaired function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior episodes, family history, chronic illness/pain, substance use, postpartum period, social isolation
Older adults: disability, bereavement, polypharmacy; somatic presentations

rows.label: Clues
items: SIGECAPS: sleep, interest, guilt, energy, concentration, appetite, psychomotor change, suicidality
Psychotic depression: delusions/hallucinations only during mood episodes, often guilt or nihilism
★ **Suicide risk**: prior attempt, intent, plan, means, agitation, psychosis, intoxication
Youth: **irritable mood** qualifies; academic decline, withdrawal, somatic complaints; not normal teenage behavior

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Multifactorial mood-circuit dysfunction involving monoamines, **HPA hyperactivity with raised cortisol**, and neuroplasticity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ MDD: **≥5 symptoms for ≥2 weeks**, including depressed mood or anhedonia; exclude mania/hypomania
Screen all adults, even asymptomatic: PHQ-2, PHQ-9 for severity; older adults: **Geriatric Depression Scale**
Interview establishes diagnosis; assess substances, drugs, TSH/CBC when clinically suspected
★ **Ask directly about suicide**, access to firearms, protective factors; questioning does not increase risk
Post-CABG anhedonia, withdrawal, fatigue → depression screen; vein-harvest leg edema expected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Imminent danger or **severe malnutrition** → **observation, psychiatric hospitalization**; remove lethal means
Mild: CBT/interpersonal therapy; moderate/severe: sertraline + psychotherapy; pregnancy → shared risk–benefit discussion
★ Urgent suicidality/catatonia/anorexia → **ECT**; psychotic depression → ECT or antidepressant + antipsychotic
Alternatives: **bupropion** (fatigue/hypersomnia, smoking cessation), **mirtazapine** (poor appetite, insomnia)
Continue antidepressant ≥6 months after remission; recurrent/severe episodes → longer maintenance

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, malnutrition, functional decline, recurrence
SSRIs: sexual dysfunction, GI effects, hyponatremia; early activation/suicidality monitoring, especially age <25
Bupropion: seizures; avoid with eating disorders, seizure disorders or brain tumor; mirtazapine: weight gain/sedation
Benzodiazepines in older adults: worsen depression, sedation, falls → stop, use antidepressant

rows.label: Prevention
items: Safety plan, early follow-up after drug changes
Taper antidepressants to reduce discontinuation symptoms; avoid antidepressant monotherapy in bipolar disorder

rows.label: Mimics
items: Dementia: insidious consistent deficits; **pseudodementia**: subacute, "I don't know" answers, recall improves with prompting
Hypothyroidism: cold intolerance, constipation, elevated TSH
Untreated OSA: snoring, obesity, sleepiness → **mood disorder due to medical condition**, not MDD
Anorexia nervosa: fear of weight gain, distorted body image

table.title: Distinguishing persistent sadness
rows: Waves tied to reminders; self-esteem usually preserved
Pervasive worthlessness; bereavement does not exclude diagnosis
Stressor within 3 months; MDD criteria absent

diverticular-disease.name: Diverticular disease
diverticular-disease.scope: Diverticulosis, acute diverticulitis, complicated diverticulitis (abscess, perforation, fistula), CT imaging, antibiotic therapy
diverticular-disease.core: Diverticulosis can bleed without pain; inflamed diverticula cause focal abdominal pain, with CT distinguishing uncomplicated disease from abscess or perforation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, obesity, smoking, low physical activity; regular NSAID use
Immunosuppression increases severity and can blunt fever or peritoneal findings

rows.label: Clues
items: Left lower quadrant tenderness, fever, leukocytosis, altered bowel habits
★ **Pneumaturia, fecaluria, recurrent polymicrobial UTI** → colovesical fistula
Peritoneal signs, hypotension, persistent vomiting → complicated disease requiring hospital evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mucosa/submucosa herniate through muscular weak points at penetrating vessels
Diverticular inflammation causes localized microperforation; adjacent vessel erosion causes arterial bleeding

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected first/severe episode → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**
Colonic wall thickening and pericolic stranding support inflammation; assess abscess, free air, obstruction
★ **Avoid colonoscopy during acute inflammation**; perforation risk
Colonoscopy after recovery for complicated disease, alarm findings, or overdue cancer screening; usually wait 6–8 weeks

rows.label: Tx
items: Low-risk uncomplicated disease: oral hydration, analgesia, advance diet as symptoms improve; antibiotics selective
★ Frail, immunocompromised, systemically ill, or complicated → **antibiotics** covering gram-negatives/anaerobes
Outpatient: amoxicillin-clavulanate (older exams: ciprofloxacin/metronidazole); severe: ceftriaxone/metronidazole or pip-tazo
Small abscess: antibiotics; larger accessible abscess, often >3 cm → percutaneous drainage
★ Peritonitis, uncontrolled sepsis, obstruction → **urgent surgery**; fistula → elective resection after stabilization

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, free perforation, stricture, fistula; recurrence does not automatically require colectomy
Severe diverticular hemorrhage may require colonoscopic hemostasis or angiographic embolization

rows.label: Prevention
items: Fiber-rich diet after recovery, exercise, weight management, smoking cessation
No need to avoid nuts, seeds, popcorn; avoid regular NSAIDs when possible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Colon cancer: progressive symptoms, weight loss, iron deficiency; can coexist
Ischemic colitis: sudden cramping then hematochezia, vascular risk
IBS: recurrent pain without fever or objective inflammation

dyslipidemia.name: Dyslipidemia
dyslipidemia.scope: Lipid screening guidelines, ASCVD risk calculation, statin therapy indications, monitoring response to diet and pharmacotherapy
dyslipidemia.core: Excess atherogenic lipoproteins drive ASCVD; treatment intensity follows established disease, severe LDL elevation, diabetes, and estimated absolute cardiovascular risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Familial disorders, saturated-fat intake, obesity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis
Premature ASCVD family history, CKD, smoking, inflammatory disease increase treatment benefit

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; tendon xanthomas/early corneal arcus suggest familial hypercholesterolemia
Severe triglyceride elevation: eruptive xanthomas, pancreatitis; low HDL alone is not a drug target

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retained apoB-containing particles → arterial inflammation and plaque formation
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase → hepatic LDL-receptor upregulation
Familial hypercholesterolemia: **defective LDL-receptor uptake** → isolated high LDL, clear plasma; high TG: milky plasma

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Lipid panel from age 19, at least every 5 years**; earlier/more often with risk
Nonfasting panel acceptable; markedly high triglycerides → fasting repeat/secondary-cause evaluation; Lp(a) once/lifetime
★ **PREVENT-ASCVD**, ages 30–79, LDL 70–189 without ASCVD: replaces pooled-cohort equations in 2026 guidance
Uncertain statin decision → coronary calcium; zero insufficient for deferral with diabetes, smoking, strong premature history
High total cholesterol alone → full lipid panel before treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Clinical ASCVD (CAD, stroke, PAD) or **LDL ≥190 mg/dL → high-intensity statin**, no risk calculation required
★ Diabetes age 40–75 → **at least moderate-intensity statin**; multiple risk factors favor high intensity
Above LDL target despite maximal statin → ezetimibe; consider PCSK9 inhibitor or bempedoic acid
Severe triglycerides ≥500 → address causes, diet, consider fenofibrate/prescription omega-3 to reduce pancreatitis risk
