Adolescent obesity + moderate LDL → **calorie reduction/lifestyle first**; statin only if severe or persistent

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, stroke, peripheral arterial disease; statins → myalgias, rare rhabdomyolysis, small diabetes-risk increase
Baseline ALT; CK only with symptoms/risk; most lipid-lowering drugs deferred during conception/pregnancy/lactation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mediterranean-style diet, replace saturated fats, exercise, weight reduction, smoking cessation
★ Recheck lipids **4–12 weeks after diet/drug change**, then every 3–12 months; high despite diet → statin
High intensity lowers LDL ≥50%: atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypothyroidism: elevated TSH; correct before labeling primary dyslipidemia
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia; treat renal cause

table.title: Risk-based primary prevention and secondary target

dyspepsia-and-peptic-ulcer-disease.name: Dyspepsia and peptic ulcer disease
dyspepsia-and-peptic-ulcer-disease.scope: Uninvestigated dyspepsia (age < 60 test-and-treat vs age >= 60 endoscopy), Helicobacter pylori testing and eradication, gastric and duodenal ulcers
dyspepsia-and-peptic-ulcer-disease.core: Epigastric discomfort may reflect functional dyspepsia or acid-peptic ulceration; age and bleeding risk determine noninvasive testing versus endoscopy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: H pylori, NSAIDs/aspirin; smoking impairs healing
Prior ulcer bleeding, anticoagulants, older age amplify NSAID harm; severe physiologic stress causes ICU ulcers

rows.label: Clues
items: Epigastric burning, early satiety, nausea; meal timing cannot reliably distinguish ulcer location
★ **Alarm**: hematemesis/melena, positive occult blood, dysphagia, persistent vomiting, weight loss, iron-deficiency anemia
Sudden rigid abdomen → perforation
Early satiety, nonbilious vomiting, succussion splash, gastric distention → gastric outlet obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: H pylori or prostaglandin depletion weakens mucosal defenses against acid-pepsin injury
Antral-predominant infection increases acid; corpus-predominant inflammation may cause atrophy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ New dyspepsia **≥60 years or any alarm feature → upper endoscopy**
★ Under 60 without concerning features → **urea breath or stool antigen test**
Hold PPI 2 weeks and antibiotics/bismuth 4 weeks before active-infection testing; serology cannot confirm eradication
Gastric ulcer → biopsy to exclude malignancy; duodenal ulcers rarely malignant
Refractory/recurrent multiple ulcers + diarrhea → fasting gastrin with careful PPI interpretation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ H pylori → **14-day bismuth quadruple**: PPI + bismuth + tetracycline + metronidazole
Avoid empiric clarithromycin/levofloxacin regimens unless susceptibility demonstrated
Negative infection test or persistent symptoms after eradication → PPI trial; functional symptoms may need TCA
Stop NSAID; ulcer healing → PPI; active bleeding → resuscitation, IV PPI, urgent endoscopic hemostasis
Perforation → IV fluids, ceftriaxone/metronidazole, urgent surgery; no elective diagnostic endoscopy

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhage, perforation, penetration, outlet obstruction from scarring/fibrosis; H pylori → gastric cancer, MALT lymphoma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Confirm eradication ≥4 weeks after antibiotics** with breath/stool test, off PPI as above
Necessary NSAID + high GI risk → concurrent PPI; use lowest effective NSAID exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Biliary colic: episodic RUQ pain, gallstones on ultrasound
ACS: exertional epigastric pressure, ischemic ECG/troponin findings

dyspepsia-and-peptic-ulcer-disease.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACG H pylori update (2024)](https://gi.org/journals-publications/ebgi/schoenfeld_sep2024/); dyspepsia age threshold established ACG/CAG teaching.

elder-abuse-and-neglect.name: Elder abuse and neglect
elder-abuse-and-neglect.scope: Physical abuse, psychological abuse, neglect, financial exploitation, clinical red flags, reporting to adult protective services
elder-abuse-and-neglect.core: Unexplained injury, unmet basic needs, intimidation, or loss of financial control warrants private assessment, safety planning, and mandated reporting.

rows.label: Principle
items: Respect autonomy while protecting vulnerable adults; decision-making capacity is specific to the decision
Dependence, cognitive impairment, isolation, caregiver strain, and coercion increase vulnerability
Genital laceration/bleeding in dependent elder → suspect sexual abuse

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Interview separately**; ask about safety, threats, caregiving, finances, basic needs
★ Stabilize injuries; assess cognition, capacity, suicidality, immediate danger, and safe disposition
★ Document quotes/findings; report suspected abuse to **Adult Protective Services**

rows.label: Don't
items: Do not confront the suspected abuser before arranging safety or disclose confidential plans unnecessarily
Do not require proof, a confession, or patient permission when reporting is legally mandatory
Poverty, accidental bruises, informed treatment refusal alone → insufficient evidence of neglect

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Immediate danger → emergency services; suspected crime may require police reporting
Capacitated adult can usually decline services; mandatory reporting may still apply under state law
Incapacity with unsafe care → protective intervention, surrogate review, possible emergency guardianship

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Inconsistent histories, different injury ages**, delayed care, controlling caregiver → investigate
Malnutrition, pressure injuries, medication deprivation → neglect; forced signatures → exploitation
Psychological abuse may leave no physical marks; arrange social work and confidential follow-up

elder-abuse-and-neglect.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics principles; reporting statutes vary by jurisdiction.

esophageal-motility-disorders.name: Esophageal motility disorders
esophageal-motility-disorders.scope: Achalasia, diffuse esophageal spasm, hypercontractile esophagus, Zenker diverticulum, manometry, barium swallow
esophageal-motility-disorders.core: Dysphagia to solids and liquids from onset suggests impaired motility; progressive solids-first dysphagia suggests mechanical obstruction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Achalasia often idiopathic; Chagas disease can destroy enteric ganglia
Older age predisposes to Zenker diverticulum; opioids can produce spastic motility patterns

rows.label: Clues
items: Achalasia: regurgitated undigested food, nocturnal cough, weight loss
★ Zenker: **halitosis, cervical gurgling, aspiration**, retained food hours after eating
Spastic disorders: intermittent dysphagia and squeezing chest pain; hot/cold liquids may provoke

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Achalasia: loss of inhibitory myenteric neurons → impaired LES relaxation and absent peristalsis
Zenker: cricopharyngeal dysfunction → mucosal herniation through Killian triangle

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Esophageal symptoms → **upper endoscopy** to exclude stricture/cancer before motility testing
★ **High-resolution manometry** confirms functional disorder after structural disease excluded
Barium swallow defines emptying; suspected Zenker → **barium study before endoscopy**
Rapid weight loss, older onset or difficult LES passage → evaluate pseudoachalasia with CT/endoscopic ultrasound
Chest pain → exclude ACS before labeling esophageal spasm

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Achalasia → pneumatic dilation, Heller myotomy + fundoplication, or **POEM**
Botulinum toxin for achalasia when procedural risk precludes durable treatment
Spastic disorders → remove opioid trigger, treat reflux; diltiazem or nitrates for persistent symptoms
Symptomatic Zenker → **cricopharyngeal myotomy + diverticulectomy** or endoscopic septotomy; no dilation or blind NG tube

rows.label: Complications
items: Aspiration pneumonia, malnutrition; longstanding achalasia → increased squamous cancer risk
Dilation/myotomy → perforation; myotomy, especially POEM → gastroesophageal reflux

rows.label: Prevention
items: Eat slowly, chew thoroughly, remain upright after meals to reduce regurgitation/aspiration

rows.label: Mimics
items: Esophageal cancer: progressive solids-first symptoms; obstructing lesion
Scleroderma: hypotensive LES with reflux, distal aperistalsis

table.title: Manometry and contrast findings
rows: Impaired LES relaxation; absent normal peristalsis

esophageal-motility-disorders.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACG achalasia guideline](https://gi.org/guideline/diagnosis-and-management-of-achalasia/); other disorders established teaching.

essential-hypertension.name: Essential hypertension
essential-hypertension.scope: Blood pressure staging, nonpharmacologic interventions (weight loss, DASH, exercise), first-line antihypertensive agents, resistant hypertension
essential-hypertension.core: Persistently elevated arterial pressure usually reflects multifactorial primary hypertension; confirm accurate repeated measurements before long-term treatment decisions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, family history, obesity, excess sodium/alcohol, inactivity, poor sleep
NSAIDs, stimulants, oral contraceptives can raise BP; assess before labeling primary disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; headache alone does not establish hypertensive emergency
★ **Acute target-organ injury** with severe pressure → hypertensive emergency; BP number alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased vascular resistance, altered renal sodium handling, sympathetic/RAAS activation sustain elevated pressure
Chronic endothelial injury accelerates atherosclerosis and small-vessel organ damage
Older adults: large-artery stiffness (low compliance) → **isolated systolic hypertension**, wide pulse pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Average ≥2 readings on ≥2 visits; confirm using **home BP or ambulatory monitoring**
Rest seated, feet supported, correct cuff, arm at heart level; avoid recent caffeine/exercise
BMP, creatinine/eGFR, urinalysis/albuminuria, lipids, glucose/A1c, ECG assess risk and injury
Resistant: above goal on 3 agents including diuretic, or controlled on ≥4; exclude pseudoresistance
Child/adolescent high oscillometric reading → **confirm by auscultation** before ambulatory monitoring or workup

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **DASH diet, weight reduction, sodium restriction, aerobic activity**, moderate alcohol; target generally <130/80
≥140/90 → drugs, usually two classes; ≥130/80 with CVD, diabetes, CKD, or PREVENT ≥7.5% → drugs
★ Low-risk stage 1: **3–6 months lifestyle**, then drugs if still ≥130/80; updated 2025 threshold
Initial: chlorthalidone, amlodipine, lisinopril, or losartan; albuminuric CKD → ACE inhibitor/ARB (older exams: any diabetes)
Resistant after optimized triple regimen → spironolactone; monitor K/creatinine; never combine ACE inhibitor + ARB

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, LV hypertrophy/HF, CKD, retinopathy, aortic disease
Thiazide: low Na/K, gout; ACE inhibitor: cough/angioedema; RAAS drugs contraindicated in pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication adherence, home readings, regular follow-up; assess orthostatic symptoms in older adults
Weight loss: largest lifestyle BP drop, ~1 mm Hg/kg; smoking cessation barely lowers resting BP
BP control: largest modifiable stroke-risk reduction; also prevents concentric LVH and HF

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: office high, home normal
Masked hypertension: elevated out-of-office only; secondary causes: abrupt/refractory pressure with renal/endocrine clues

gastrointestinal-bleeding.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding
gastrointestinal-bleeding.scope: Upper GI bleeding (PUD, varices, Mallory-Weiss), lower GI bleeding (diverticular, angiodysplasia, hemorrhoids), fluid and transfusion thresholds, endoscopy
gastrointestinal-bleeding.core: Hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia → assess hemodynamics before localizing; brisk upper bleeding can present as bright red rectal blood.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: NSAIDs/H pylori → ulcers; cirrhosis → varices; forceful retching → mucosal tear
Anticoagulants/antiplatelets increase severity; older age favors diverticula or angiodysplasia

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Syncope, orthostasis, shock** signal major loss; initial hemoglobin may remain normal
Epigastric pain supports ulcer; painless bleeding favors vascular sources
Recurrent occult loss → iron deficiency
**Melena**, elevated BUN/creatinine ratio → upper source; bilious NG aspirate argues against upper bleeding

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mucosal injury, portal-pressure collaterals, or fragile vessels rupture into GI lumen
Volume depletion → reduced perfusion; ongoing bleeding may require massive transfusion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Two large-bore IVs, CBC, type/cross, coagulation tests**, serial hemoglobin; resuscitate before procedures
Upper source → EGD within 24 hours after stabilization; suspected varices → within 12 hours
★ Ongoing hemodynamically significant hematochezia → **CT angiography → embolization** if active extravasation
Stable lower bleeding → bowel preparation and nonemergent colonoscopy; routine <24-hour colonoscopy adds no benefit
Rectal bleeding mixed with stool, age ≥45 → colonoscopy; negative FOBT does not exclude neoplasia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Crystalloid initially; stable nonischemic adults → **RBC transfusion at hemoglobin <7 g/dL**
Exsanguination or post-crystalloid shock → **RBCs** regardless of hemoglobin, not vasopressors; cardiac ischemia → higher threshold
Severe anticoagulant bleeding → drug-specific reversal; uncontrolled varices → balloon tamponade as temporary bridge only
Failed endoscopy → IR/surgery; massive unlocalized lower bleeding → **total abdominal colectomy**, not segmental
Suspected ulcer → IV PPI; endoscopic hemostasis for active bleeding/visible vessel, then high-dose PPI

rows.label: Complications
items: Rebleeding, aspiration, myocardial ischemia, AKI; variceal bleeding → infection
Massive transfusion → hypocalcemia, hypothermia, coagulopathy; embolization → bowel ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Eradicate H pylori and confirm cure; avoid NSAIDs; PPI for high-risk users
After variceal control: nonselective beta-blocker plus repeat banding; recurrent bleeding → TIPS

rows.label: Mimics
items: Iron/bismuth: dark stool without blood loss
Hemoptysis: coughing frothy blood rather than vomiting
Swallowed epistaxis: nasal source on examination

table.title: Source-specific branches
rows: Postretching tear; Boerhaave instead: chest pain, crepitus
Liver trauma + jaundice; blood from ampulla

gastrointestinal-bleeding.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACG lower GI bleeding 2023](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36735555/), [ACS transfusion guidance 2025](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2024.11.009).

generalized-anxiety-disorder.name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
generalized-anxiety-disorder.scope: GAD diagnostic criteria, pharmacotherapy (SSRIs, SNRIs, buspirone), psychotherapy (CBT), differential diagnosis
generalized-anxiety-disorder.core: Difficult-to-control worry about multiple everyday domains on most days for at least 6 months causes distress or functional impairment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family anxiety history, chronic stress, trauma, female sex, comorbid depression
Caffeine, stimulants, thyroid hormone excess, and substance withdrawal can reproduce symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Adults: **≥3** of restlessness, fatigue, poor concentration, irritability, muscle tension, sleep disturbance
Children require only one associated symptom; reassurance provides limited sustained relief
Worries shift among health, family, work, and finances rather than one circumscribed trigger
Assess suicidality, substance use, depressive symptoms, and manic history before treatment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Heightened threat appraisal and impaired fear regulation perpetuate autonomic arousal and anticipatory worry
Avoidance and reassurance-seeking reinforce anxiety, providing targets for cognitive and behavioral interventions

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis** after excluding substance effects and medical explanations
GAD-7 quantifies severity and response; not a substitute for diagnostic interview
TSH, ECG, or other testing guided by tremor, weight change, palpitations, or examination
Symptoms confined to another disorder, such as obsessions or trauma reminders, favor that diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **CBT** targets cognitive distortions, avoidance, and worry; exercise and sleep regularity support recovery
★ Persistent impairment → **SSRI** such as escitalopram/sertraline, or SNRI such as venlafaxine/duloxetine
Buspirone: scheduled nonbenzodiazepine option; delayed onset, low dependence risk, not useful as needed
Allow several weeks at therapeutic dose; continue effective treatment after remission, then taper gradually
Benzodiazepines: brief selected bridging only; avoid chronic use, especially with opioids or fall risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Depression, impaired function, substance misuse; benzodiazepine dependence and withdrawal
SSRIs/SNRIs: GI effects, sexual dysfunction, early activation; SNRIs may increase BP

rows.label: Prevention
items: Reduce caffeine/stimulants, practice CBT skills, monitor relapse during medication taper
Address chronic stress and comorbid sleep, mood, or substance-use disorders

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic disorder: discrete abrupt attacks with anticipatory fear
Adjustment disorder: stressor-linked symptoms beginning within 3 months
Hyperthyroidism: heat intolerance, weight loss, tremor, suppressed TSH

generalized-anxiety-disorder.evidence: Not checked online; established psychiatric diagnostic and treatment teaching.

gestational-diabetes-mellitus.name: Gestational diabetes mellitus
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Screening (50g oral glucose challenge at 24-28 weeks), diagnostic 3-hour 100g test, glycemic targets, nutritional therapy, insulin, fetal and neonatal complications (macrosomia, hypoglycemia, RDS, polycythemia)
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.core: Pregnancy-induced insulin resistance unmasks hyperglycemia, increasing fetal insulin secretion and growth; screen routinely at 24–28 weeks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, prior GDM/macrosomia, family history of type 2 diabetes, PCOS
High-risk patients need early assessment for previously unrecognized overt diabetes

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; excessive fetal growth or polyhydramnios may prompt evaluation
Early marked hyperglycemia suggests preexisting diabetes rather than typical later-onset GDM

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental hormones increase maternal insulin requirements; inadequate beta-cell compensation causes dysglycemia
Maternal glucose crosses placenta; insulin does not; fetal hyperinsulinemia persists briefly after birth
Fetal hyperinsulinemia → macrosomia; antagonizes cortisol → less surfactant, **RDS**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Two-step screen: **nonfasting 50 g challenge**, 1-hour threshold 130–140 mg/dL by local protocol
Positive challenge → fasting 100 g, 3-hour OGTT; **≥2 abnormal values** diagnose GDM
Alternative one-step 75 g OGTT: fasting ≥92, 1-hour ≥180, or 2-hour ≥153 mg/dL
HbA1c alone does not replace pregnancy glucose testing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First: **individualized nutrition, activity, home glucose monitoring**; avoid severe carbohydrate restriction
★ Targets: fasting **<95**, 1-hour <140, or 2-hour <120 mg/dL
Above targets despite lifestyle → **insulin preferred**; metformin crosses placenta, counsel if used
Medication need or poor control → fetal surveillance; delivery timing depends on control and obstetric findings
Suspected fetal weight ≥4,500 g with diabetes → discuss planned cesarean

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal: preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, future type 2 diabetes
Fetal: macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, birth trauma; poor control increases stillbirth risk
Neonate: **hypoglycemia**, RDS, polycythemia, jaundice; congenital anomalies mainly reflect pregestational diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Postpartum **75 g OGTT at 4–12 weeks**; lifelong diabetes testing every 1–3 years
Breastfeeding, weight management, activity; most GDM insulin needs resolve after placental delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pregestational diabetes: overt diagnostic-range hyperglycemia early in pregnancy
Physiologic glycosuria: lower renal threshold without diagnostic blood glucose abnormalities

gout.name: Gout and crystal arthropathy
gout.scope: Acute gout, chronic gout and urate lowering, pseudogout (CPPD)
gout.core: Abrupt intensely painful inflammatory arthritis from crystal deposition; gout and CPPD require different long-term prevention despite similar flare management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gout: CKD, obesity, alcohol, purines/fructose, thiazide/loop diuretics, low-dose aspirin
CPPD: older age, joint injury, hyperparathyroidism, hemochromatosis, hypomagnesemia
Flares follow surgery, dehydration, illness, or changes in urate concentration

rows.label: Clues
items: Rapid-onset red swollen tender joint, often overnight; fever possible
Chronic gout: tophi on ears/olecranon, erosive arthritis; recurrent flares separated by asymptomatic intervals
CPPD in younger adults → investigate associated metabolic disorders

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Crystal phagocytosis activates inflammasome/IL-1 → neutrophilic synovitis
Most hyperuricemia reflects reduced renal urate excretion rather than excessive production

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First/atypical acute monoarthritis → **arthrocentesis**, polarized microscopy, Gram stain/culture
★ **Crystals do not exclude septic arthritis**; serum urate may be normal during gout flare
Chronic imaging: punched-out defects with overhanging edges; ultrasound double-contour sign supports urate deposition

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute crystal flare → **indomethacin/other NSAID, colchicine, or glucocorticoid**; joint steroid after excluding infection
NSAID failure → switch class; older exam questions may expect potent NSAID, e.g. indomethacin
CKD/ulcer/anticoagulation → favor steroid; adjust colchicine for renal impairment/interactions; avoid NSAIDs in advanced CKD
★ Urate lowering: **allopurinol first-line**, including CKD; start low, titrate to serum urate <6 mg/dL
Urate lowering doesn't treat flares; continue through flares; may start mid-flare (older exam questions: wait)

rows.label: Complications
items: Gout: destructive arthritis, uric-acid stones; CPPD: chronic degenerative/inflammatory arthropathy
Allopurinol hypersensitivity; colchicine → diarrhea/neuromyopathy
Xanthine-oxidase inhibitors + azathioprine/6-MP → severe marrow suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Urate lowering: **tophi, joint damage, ≥2 flares/year**; first flare with CKD ≥3/stones/urate >9 → consider
Starting urate lowering → colchicine/NSAID prophylaxis 3–6 months; serial urate monitoring; not for isolated hyperuricemia
Uncomplicated first flare → **limit alcohol/fructose**, lose weight; thiazide → losartan; keep indicated aspirin
Before allopurinol: HLA-B*58:01 testing with Southeast Asian/African American ancestry; CPPD lacks crystal-depleting drugs

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic arthritis: positive culture, bacteremia risk; aspiration essential when uncertain
Cellulitis: superficial inflammation, less restriction of passive joint motion
RA: persistent symmetric small-joint synovitis

gout.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACR gout guideline 2020](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10563586/), [ACR gout education 2025](https://rheumatology.org/patients/gout); CPPD established teaching.

head-and-neck-cancer.name: Head and neck cancer
head-and-neck-cancer.scope: Oral cavity cancer, laryngeal cancer, pharyngeal cancer, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, tobacco and alcohol risk, HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma
head-and-neck-cancer.core: Persistent hoarseness, unilateral throat/ear symptoms, a nonhealing oral lesion, or an adult neck mass requires malignancy evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Tobacco, alcohol: each independent, dose-dependent squamous cancer risk, synergistic together; betel nut in some populations
HPV exposure drives many oropharyngeal cancers; EBV associated with nasopharyngeal carcinoma

rows.label: Clues
items: Oral ulcer or red/white plaque persisting >2–3 weeks; dysphagia, odynophagia, weight loss
★ **Adult persistent lateral neck mass** may be metastatic carcinoma, even when cystic
Unilateral referred otalgia with normal otoscopy; hemoptysis or stridor indicates advanced local disease
Nasopharyngeal disease → unilateral serous otitis, epistaxis or cranial neuropathy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mucosal squamous transformation and lymphatic spread; field carcinogenesis produces synchronous/second primary tumors

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Direct visualization and biopsy** of mucosal lesion; flexible nasolaryngoscopy for inaccessible sites
Neck mass → contrast CT/MRI plus **fine-needle aspiration**; avoid initial open biopsy
Oropharyngeal tumor → p16/HPV testing; staging imaging assesses regional nodes and distant metastases
Persistent hoarseness → laryngoscopy; no prolonged empiric reflux treatment when malignancy clues present

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Airway compromise/stridor → **secure airway** with ENT/anesthesia support
Early localized cancer → surgery or radiation according to site and function
Locally advanced → combined surgery/radiation with cisplatin-based systemic treatment or definitive chemoradiation
Nasopharyngeal cancer → chemoradiation; recurrent/metastatic disease → systemic treatment, often checkpoint inhibitor

rows.label: Complications
items: Aspiration, airway obstruction, malnutrition, carotid bleeding; nodal/distant metastases
Radiation → xerostomia, dental decay, osteoradionecrosis; surgery → speech/swallow impairment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Smoking/alcohol cessation, HPV vaccination; dental assessment before head/neck radiation
Swallowing rehabilitation, nutrition support; surveillance for recurrence and second primary cancer

rows.label: Mimics
items: Laryngitis: brief postviral hoarseness resolving with recovery
Branchial cleft cyst: benign developmental lesion; new adult cystic mass still needs cancer exclusion

head-and-neck-cancer.evidence: Neck-mass evaluation checked 2026-10-30: [AAO-HNS adult neck-mass guideline](https://www.entnet.org/quality-practice/quality-products/clinical-practice-guidelines/evaluation-of-the-neck-mass-in-adults/); oncology: established teaching.

hearing-loss.name: Hearing loss
hearing-loss.scope: Conductive vs sensorineural hearing loss, Weber and Rinne tests, presbycusis, ototoxicity (cisplatin, aminoglycosides, loop diuretics), noise-induced, Meniere disease, acoustic neuroma
hearing-loss.core: Distinguish impaired sound conduction from cochlear/nerve dysfunction; sudden sensorineural loss requires urgent treatment rather than observation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Aging, occupational/recreational noise, cerumen, chronic middle-ear disease
★ Ototoxins: **cisplatin, aminoglycosides, loop diuretics**; risk increases with renal impairment and combined exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: Presbycusis: bilateral high-frequency loss, difficulty understanding speech amid background noise
Noise injury: high-frequency audiometric notch; tinnitus common
Ménière: episodic vertigo, fluctuating low-frequency loss, tinnitus, aural fullness
★ **Unilateral progressive loss + poor speech discrimination** → vestibular schwannoma; imbalance may accompany

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Conductive: external/middle-ear transmission impaired; sensorineural: cochlea or auditory nerve damaged
Chronic noise/aging preferentially damages basal cochlear hair cells; Ménière involves endolymphatic hydrops

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Otoscopy → tuning forks → formal audiometry**, including air/bone thresholds and speech testing
Tympanometry evaluates middle-ear mechanics; asymmetric sensorineural loss → MRI internal auditory canals
Sudden loss: ≥30 dB across ≥3 contiguous frequencies within 72 hours; urgent audiogram/ENT
Do not attribute sudden unilateral deficit to cerumen without confirming resolution after removal

rows.label: Tx
items: Remove cerumen, treat effusion/infection or structural cause; persistent conductive disease → ENT
★ Sudden sensorineural loss → **corticosteroids promptly**, within 2 weeks; intratympanic route possible
Chronic bilateral deficit → hearing aids, communication strategies; severe refractory loss → cochlear implant evaluation
Ménière: sodium moderation, selected diuretic; short-term vestibular suppressant during attacks
Vestibular schwannoma: observation, stereotactic radiation, or surgery according to tumor size and symptoms

rows.label: Complications
items: Communication barriers, social isolation, depression, impaired safety awareness
Ototoxicity can be permanent; vestibular injury can cause imbalance and falls

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hearing protection, safe listening levels, baseline/serial audiometry with ototoxic drugs

rows.label: Mimics
items: Auditory processing/cognitive disorder: difficulty understanding despite relatively preserved peripheral thresholds
BPPV: brief positional vertigo without hearing loss

heat-related-illness.name: Heat-related illness
heat-related-illness.scope: Heat exhaustion, classic and exertional heat stroke, malignant hyperthermia and NMS contrast
heat-related-illness.core: Heat exposure with neurologic dysfunction signals heat stroke, requiring immediate cooling before laboratory confirmation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Classic: older adults (**impaired thirst**), heat waves, impaired sweating, anticholinergics, limited water access
Exertional: strenuous activity, poor acclimatization, heavy equipment, stimulant use

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Delirium, seizures, or coma** distinguish heat stroke from uncomplicated heat exhaustion
Tachycardia, hypotension, vomiting; sweating may persist despite severe heat injury
Core temperature often >40 °C; lower readings after cooling do not exclude heat stroke

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Heat production exceeds dissipation → endothelial injury, systemic inflammation, cellular dysfunction
Sweat losses → hypovolemia; excessive free water intake can produce hyponatremia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Rectal temperature**; oral, axillary, and tympanic measurements may underestimate severity
CBC, electrolytes, creatinine, CK, urinalysis, liver enzymes, coagulation studies; repeat for evolving injury

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Airway support, remove clothing, **rapid whole-body cooling**; do not delay for transport or tests
Exertional: cold-water immersion, else evaporative cooling; classic: evaporative; no alcohol sponging; stop active cooling near 39 °C
★ **IV isotonic crystalloid** for hypovolemia; benzodiazepines for seizures or shivering
Avoid antipyretics; environmental hyperthermia has no elevated hypothalamic temperature set point

rows.label: Complications
items: Rhabdomyolysis, AKI, DIC, hepatic failure, ARDS, persistent neurologic deficits
Delayed liver injury despite initial clinical improvement

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Gradual acclimatization**, scheduled rest, shade, hydration, cooling access
Avoid strenuous exercise during peak heat; monitor vulnerable adults during heat waves

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sepsis: infectious focus, fever unrelated to environmental load
Serotonin syndrome: serotonergic exposure, clonus, hyperreflexia

heat-related-illness.evidence: Not checked online; established emergency medicine teaching.

hiv-infection.name: HIV infection
hiv-infection.scope: Acute HIV, testing, ART start, opportunistic infection prophylaxis, PrEP/PEP, opportunistic infections (CMV retinitis, toxoplasmosis, PJP)
hiv-infection.core: HIV progressively depletes CD4 cells; early diagnosis and suppressive ART prevent immune failure and sexual transmission.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual exposure, shared injection equipment, perinatal transmission; other STIs increase acquisition risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Acute infection 2–4 weeks post-exposure: fever, rash, sore throat, **mucosal ulcers**, diarrhea, generalized lymphadenopathy
Weight loss, thrush, recurrent candida/herpes, **extensive adult molluscum** → test HIV; dysphagia → candidal esophagitis
Child/teen: chronic fever/diarrhea, poor growth, generalized nodes, splenomegaly, **polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retroviral integration creates lifelong reservoirs; ongoing replication drives immune depletion and inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Fourth-generation Ag/Ab → HIV-1/2 differentiation assay**; discordance → HIV RNA
★ Recent exposure/acute syndrome despite negative screen → **HIV RNA**, before antibodies appear
Baseline viral load, CD4, genotype, renal/liver function, HBV/HCV/TB, pregnancy testing, **cervical cytology**
AIDS: CD4 <200 or AIDS-defining illness regardless of count
Prenatal: opt-out screening; refusal → counsel, re-offer later; never test without consent

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Start **integrase-based ART promptly**, usually bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine; assess HBV coinfection and interactions
Do not delay routine ART for genotype; cryptococcal/TB meningitis require disease-specific deferred timing
PJP: TMP-SMX; add glucocorticoid if PaO₂ <70 or A–a gradient ≥35
Toxoplasmosis: **pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine/leucovorin**, else TMP-SMX; CMV retinitis: valganciclovir, ophthalmology
Untreated/viremic mother's newborn → **triple ART** ASAP, ideally within 6 h, ≤6 weeks; suppressed mother → zidovudine alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Opportunistic infections, malignancies, wasting, neurocognitive disease, kidney disease
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome after ART; drug toxicity/interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ PJP prophylaxis: **TMP-SMX** with CD4 <200 before/starting ART; on ART, <100 or 100–200 with viremia
Toxoplasma IgG positive + CD4 <100 → prophylaxis; MAC <50 only without immediate effective ART
★ Exposure ≤72 hours → **28-day PEP: dolutegravir + TDF/emtricitabine**; do not delay for laboratory results
PrEP: TDF/emtricitabine, cabotegravir, or lenacapavir; exclude HIV first, continue serial testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: EBV mononucleosis: atypical lymphocytes, heterophile positivity; acute HIV can be heterophile-negative
Primary CNS lymphoma: often solitary lesion; biopsy after failed empiric anti-Toxoplasma treatment, earlier if serology/imaging/CSF PCR disagree
SCID/CVID: low immunoglobulins; SCID lymphopenia, no nodes; perinatal HIV: PJP, thrush, nodes, normal lymphocytes

table.title: Advanced-disease syndromes
rows: Dry cough, hypoxemia, ground-glass; sputum/BAL silver stain
Ring-enhancing mass lesions, edema/mass effect; positive IgG
Cognitive decline; non-enhancing subcortical demyelination, no mass effect

hypersensitivity-pneumonitis.name: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
hypersensitivity-pneumonitis.scope: Bird fancier lung, farmer lung, acute vs chronic presentation, antigen avoidance, centrilobular ground-glass nodules on HRCT, systemic corticosteroids
hypersensitivity-pneumonitis.core: Immune-mediated small-airway and interstitial lung disease follows inhaled antigen exposure; identifying and removing the exposure is central to treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Bird proteins from pets, feathers, droppings; moldy hay in farming
Damp buildings, contaminated humidifiers/hot tubs, occupational organic dust; ask about home and hobbies

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Recurrent **cough, dyspnea, fever hours after exposure**, improvement away from source
Chronic exposure: insidious exertional limitation, weight loss, dry inspiratory crackles; clubbing with fibrosis
Hypoxemia, tachypnea, falling exercise saturation indicate substantial impairment; chronic disease may lack febrile episodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Repeated antigen inhalation triggers immune-complex and T-cell responses around bronchioles and alveoli
Persistent inflammation produces poorly formed noncaseating granulomas and potentially irreversible fibrosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Exposure history + HRCT**: centrilobular ground-glass nodules, mosaic attenuation, expiratory air trapping
Fibrotic disease: reticulation, traction bronchiectasis ± honeycombing; distribution can differ from basal-predominant IPF
PFTs: restriction and ↓DLCO, sometimes mixed obstruction; BAL lymphocytosis supports diagnosis
Serum antigen-specific IgG documents sensitization, **not disease**; absence does not exclude
Multidisciplinary review; biopsy only when exposure, imaging, and BAL leave clinically important uncertainty

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Complete antigen avoidance** and environmental remediation; respirator alone may be insufficient
★ Severe symptomatic nonfibrotic disease → **systemic glucocorticoids** to accelerate recovery
Oxygen for hypoxemia, pulmonary rehabilitation; progressive fibrotic disease → specialist antifibrotic consideration
Advanced refractory fibrosis → lung transplant evaluation; antibiotics do not treat sterile immune inflammation

rows.label: Complications
items: Progressive fibrosis, pulmonary hypertension, chronic respiratory failure, cor pulmonale
Symptoms can persist despite avoidance once irreversible structural damage has occurred

rows.label: Prevention
items: Remove birds/mold sources, maintain ventilation, control workplace organic-dust exposure
Counsel household members about ongoing feather products or hidden dampness; monitor lung function after removal

rows.label: Mimics
items: IPF: older adult, basal subpleural honeycombing, no explanatory antigen
Sarcoidosis: well-formed granulomas, hilar adenopathy, extrapulmonary involvement
Organic dust toxic syndrome: heavy exposure, acute flu-like illness without antigen-specific sensitization

hypersensitivity-pneumonitis.evidence: Not checked online; established ATS diagnostic and management teaching.

hyperthyroidism.name: Hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis
hyperthyroidism.scope: Graves disease, toxic multinodular goiter, toxic adenoma, subacute thyroiditis, thyroid storm, beta-blockers, thionamides, radioactive iodine
hyperthyroidism.core: Excess circulating thyroid hormone → heat intolerance, weight loss despite appetite, tremor, and tachycardia; hormone overproduction differs from destructive release.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune history, female sex; older age favors autonomous nodules
Iodine load, amiodarone, exogenous thyroid hormone; infection/surgery can precipitate storm

rows.label: Clues
items: Hyperreflexia, lid lag, onycholysis, frequent stools, proximal weakness, widened pulse pressure; older adults: apathetic
★ **Thyroid storm**: fever, delirium, severe tachyarrhythmia, vomiting, heart failure; clinical diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased tissue metabolic activity and beta-adrenergic sensitivity explain systemic manifestations
Thionamides block thyroid peroxidase; PTU also reduces peripheral T4 → T3 conversion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH first → free T4**, total T3 if T4 normal; suppressed TSH with elevated hormones
TRAb establishes Graves; uncertain cause → **Doppler ultrasound** or radioiodine uptake (not if pregnant/lactating)
Low uptake: thyroiditis/exogenous hormone; low thyroglobulin supports exogenous ingestion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptom control: **propranolol**; caution in asthma or decompensated HF
★ Storm → ICU, cooling/fluids, beta-blockade if tolerated, **PTU → iodine ≥1 hour later**, hydrocortisone
Radioiodine contraindicated during pregnancy/lactation; significant active orbitopathy favors another definitive treatment
Compression/suspicious nodule → thyroidectomy after control; pregnancy: first-trimester PTU, later methimazole

rows.label: Complications
items: AF, embolism, osteoporosis, mild hypercalcemia, cardiomyopathy; radioiodine often → hypothyroidism
★ Thionamides: **fever/sore throat → stop drug, urgent CBC**; PTU → severe hepatotoxicity
Pregnancy: thionamides/TRAb cross placenta → **fetal goiter**, impaired swallowing, polyhydramnios

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor free T4 early during treatment; TSH recovery lags
Smoking cessation for orbitopathy; definitive treatment before planned pregnancy when feasible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic disorder: episodic symptoms without thyroid biochemical abnormalities
Pheochromocytoma: paroxysmal headache, sweating, severe hypertension
Menopause: hot flashes with menstrual transition, normal thyroid testing
Orbital pseudotumor: involves muscle bellies and tendons; Graves spares tendons

table.title: Etiology determines treatment
rows: Diffuse uptake; bruit, orbitopathy, pretibial myxedema, acropachy (clubbing)
One hot nodule, suppressed surrounding tissue
NSAID; prednisone if severe; no thionamides

hypoglycemia.name: Hypoglycemia
hypoglycemia.scope: Drug-induced hypoglycemia (insulin, sulfonylureas), Whipple triad, acute management (dextrose, glucagon), insulinoma
hypoglycemia.core: Compatible symptoms, documented low plasma glucose, and relief with correction establish Whipple triad and justify evaluation for a hypoglycemic disorder.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Insulin, sulfonylureas; missed meals, exercise, alcohol, kidney failure increase risk
Sepsis, liver failure, adrenal insufficiency; insulinoma causes fasting episodes in otherwise well adults
Child, illness, poor intake or sugar-free fluids → **glycogen depletion**, ketotic hypoglycemia ± anion-gap acidosis

rows.label: Clues
items: Adrenergic: tremor, sweating, palpitations, hunger; neuroglycopenic: confusion, visual change, seizures, coma
Autonomic neuropathy or recurrent episodes may blunt warning symptoms
★ Glucose **<54 mg/dL** clinically significant; diabetes alert threshold <70 mg/dL

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Excess insulin suppresses glucose output and ketones; substrate/hormone deficits impair counterregulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Bedside glucose immediately**; plasma confirmation if discordant, never delay emergency correction
Critical sample: glucose, insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin, β-hydroxybutyrate, sulfonylurea screen
Suspected endogenous fasting disorder → supervised fast up to 72 h; mixed-meal test for postprandial symptoms
Biochemically confirmed insulinoma → pancreatic CT/MRI, endoscopic ultrasound if localization unclear

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Awake and swallowing → **15 g rapid carbohydrate**, recheck after 15 minutes, repeat if needed
★ Altered or unable to swallow → **IV dextrose**; no IV access → IM/intranasal glucagon
After recovery → longer-acting carbohydrate; glucagon less effective after alcohol or glycogen depletion
★ Sulfonylurea recurrence → **octreotide + dextrose**, prolonged observation; long-acting insulin may require infusion
Adjust diabetes regimen and treat trigger; localized insulinoma → surgical resection

rows.label: Complications
items: Seizures, brain injury, arrhythmias, falls; recurrent episodes cause impaired awareness
Dextrose alone after sulfonylurea exposure may stimulate further insulin release

rows.label: Prevention
items: Meal/exercise planning, glucose monitoring or CGM alarms, caregiver rescue-glucagon education
Relax overly intensive targets when recurrent events, frailty, or impaired awareness

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic attack: normal glucose during symptoms
Stroke: focal deficit may persist after glucose correction; evaluate both if unresolved

hypoglycemia.evidence: Not checked online; established endocrine diagnostic and hypoglycemia treatment principles.

hyponatremia.name: Hyponatremia
hyponatremia.scope: Hypovolemic, euvolemic (SIADH, primary polydipsia), hypervolemic, acute vs chronic, hypertonic saline indications
hyponatremia.core: Low serum sodium reflects excess water relative to sodium; symptoms and duration determine urgency before the cause determines maintenance treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Thiazides, SSRIs, carbamazepine/oxcarbazepine, oxytocin; **hypotonic IV D5W**, postoperative state, exercise + excess water
Pulmonary/CNS disease; **small cell lung cancer** (ectopic ADH); heart failure, cirrhosis, renal failure

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, headache, gait instability; seizures, coma or marked confusion indicate severe cerebral edema
Orthostasis/dry mucosa suggest depletion; edema/ascites suggest excess extracellular fluid
SIADH: clinically euvolemic with inappropriately concentrated urine despite hypo-osmolality
Massive water intake, often psychiatric illness; urine osmolality below serum still favors polydipsia, even if >100

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hypotonic extracellular fluid drives water into brain; chronic adaptation makes rapid correction dangerous
ADH-mediated water retention or intake exceeding renal dilution capacity lowers sodium concentration
Low effective volume (heart failure, cirrhosis, diarrhea) → baroreceptor ADH release; total-body sodium high in edema

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Serum osmolality first: **<275 mOsm/kg** confirms hypotonicity; assess glucose and volume status
Hyperglycemia → translocational hyponatremia; severe hyperlipidemia/proteinemia → pseudohyponatremia
★ Urine osmolality **<100** → polydipsia/low solute; ≥100 → persistent ADH activity
Urine Na <20–30 suggests low effective arterial volume; >30 suggests renal loss or SIADH
Exclude adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism and renal failure before diagnosing SIADH; diuretics confound urine Na

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe neurologic symptoms → **3% saline bolus**, repeated for initial Na rise 4–6 mEq/L
Hypovolemia → isotonic saline; SIADH → fluid restriction, increased solute, remove trigger
Edematous states → fluid/sodium restriction and loop diuretic; treat heart/liver/kidney disorder
★ Chronic/unknown duration: generally limit rise to **≤8 mEq/L per 24 h**; monitor frequently
Overcorrection → desmopressin plus D5W; avoid routine vaptans in acute symptomatic cases

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute severe hyponatremia → herniation, respiratory arrest
Osmotic demyelination after rapid correction; greatest risk with alcoholism, malnutrition, hypokalemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid hypotonic maintenance fluids during high ADH states; review causative drugs
Monitor for brisk aquaresis after restoring volume or stopping thiazides

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cerebral salt wasting: neurosurgical patient, hypovolemic, high urine Na; SIADH euvolemic
Hyperosmolar hyperglycemia: measured osmolality elevated
Primary psychiatric disease: neurologic change without sodium abnormality

hyponatremia.evidence: Not checked online; established hyponatremia consensus principles.

hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.name: Hypothesis testing and statistical tests
hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.scope: Null and alternative hypotheses, Type I and Type II errors, statistical power, confidence intervals, p-values, t-tests (paired, unpaired), ANOVA, chi-square, Pearson correlation
hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.core: Hypothesis tests quantify incompatibility with a null model; confidence intervals describe effect estimates and uncertainty.

rows.label: Definition
items: H0: no difference/association; H1: specified difference or association
★ **α**: false-positive probability; Type I error rejects a true null
★ **β**: false-negative probability; Type II error misses a real effect

rows.label: Formula
items: Power = **1 − β**; increases with sample size, effect size, α, lower variability
95% CI ≈ estimate ± 1.96 × standard error; plausible range for true effect

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **p-value**: probability of equally/more extreme data assuming H0; not probability H0 true
95% CI excludes 0 for differences or 1 for ratios → two-sided p <0.05

rows.label: Use when
items: Pearson r: linear association between continuous variables; range −1 to +1
Ordinal/non-normal independent data → Mann–Whitney; paired → Wilcoxon signed-rank

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Nonsignificant ≠ equivalent; statistical significance ≠ clinical importance
Repeated comparisons inflate false positives; prespecify outcomes or adjust α
Correlation neither establishes causation nor detects every nonlinear relationship

hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.evidence: Statistical definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

impaired-physician.name: Impaired physician
impaired-physician.scope: Acute impairment, substance use, patient safety protection, physician health programs, mandatory reporting to state medical board
impaired-physician.core: Patient safety first when a colleague's ability to practice safely is compromised.

rows.label: Principle
items: Impairment = functional inability to practice safely from illness, substances, or cognitive decline

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Acute intoxication → stop patient contact, arrange coverage, notify supervisor immediately
★ Document objective observations and affected encounters through institutional channels
★ **Physician health program** → evaluation, treatment, monitoring, and safe return to practice

rows.label: Don't
items: Conceal unsafe care or delay intervention while seeking definitive proof
Permit impaired colleague to drive home

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Report to **state medical board** when law requires or ongoing danger remains unaddressed
PHP confidentiality and reporting exemptions vary by jurisdiction

rows.label: Traps
items: Substance use history or treatment alone ≠ current impairment
Employee assistance referral alone insufficient during an immediate patient safety threat

impaired-physician.evidence: Checked AMA Code of Medical Ethics Opinion 9.3.2.

infertility.name: Infertility
infertility.scope: Definition (failure to conceive after 12 months), initial evaluation, semen analysis (male factor), ovulatory status (midluteal progesterone), tubal and uterine factors (hysterosalpingography), ovarian reserve testing
infertility.core: No conception after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse; evaluate after 6 months at age ≥35, immediately over 40 or with risks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, PCOS, endometriosis, PID, pelvic surgery, chemotherapy, testicular injury, exogenous testosterone
Smoking, marked weight extremes, premature ovarian insufficiency, untreated endocrine disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Irregular/absent cycles → ovulatory dysfunction; galactorrhea → hyperprolactinemia; hot flashes → ovarian insufficiency
Prior ectopic pregnancy or chlamydia → tubal damage; normal cycles do not exclude male factor

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Failure of sperm production/delivery, oocyte release, fertilization, transport, or implantation; mixed factors common
Estrogen → proliferative endometrium; LH surge → ovulation
Corpus luteum **progesterone** → secretory endometrium, ↑basal body temperature

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Evaluate **both partners simultaneously**; reproductive history, sexual timing, examinations; semen analysis early
Abnormal semen result → repeat and male reproductive evaluation; do not begin with female laparoscopy
★ Ovulation uncertain → **progesterone about 7 days before expected menses**; >3 ng/mL supports ovulation
Regular 21–35-day cycles usually imply ovulation; targeted TSH, prolactin only for relevant symptoms
★ Ovulatory + normal semen → **HSG** (tubes) before laparoscopy; saline sonography: cavity; avoid in pregnancy/infection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Anovulation/PCOS → **letrozole**, clomiphene alternative; hyperprolactinemia → cabergoline; correct thyroid disease
Tubal occlusion/severe male factor → IVF, sometimes intracytoplasmic sperm injection
Unexplained infertility → ovarian stimulation with intrauterine insemination, then IVF if unsuccessful
Intercourse every 1–2 days during fertile window; avoid testosterone for fertility-seeking men

rows.label: Complications
items: Psychological distress; stimulation → ovarian hyperstimulation, multiple gestation; assisted reproduction → ectopic pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: STI prevention, tobacco cessation, weight optimization; fertility preservation before gonadotoxic treatment
Preconception folic acid and medication review

rows.label: Mimics
items: Infrequent intercourse: inadequate exposure despite normal reproductive testing
Recurrent pregnancy loss: conception occurs, followed by repeated losses

table.title: Ovarian reserve: treatment response, not natural fertility
rows: Low values suggest reduced follicular pool

infertility.evidence: Evaluation checked 2026-10-30: [ASRM 2021](https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/fertility-evaluation-of-infertile-women-a-committee-opinion-2021/); treatment established reproductive guidance.

inflammatory-bowel-disease.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
inflammatory-bowel-disease.scope: Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis, extraintestinal manifestations (erythema nodosum, pyoderma gangrenosum, uveitis), toxic megacolon, colorectal cancer risk, biologic therapy
inflammatory-bowel-disease.core: Chronic relapsing intestinal inflammation: Crohn disease affects any gastrointestinal segment; ulcerative colitis begins in the rectum.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, young adulthood; smoking worsens Crohn disease
NSAIDs and enteric infections can precipitate flares

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss, anemia; children may have growth failure
Arthritis, uveitis; PSC particularly associated with UC
Erythema nodosum: tender nonulcerating nodules; **pyoderma gangrenosum**: rapid painful violaceous ulcer, purulent base
★ Severe colitis: fever, tachycardia, frequent bloody stools; distention, colon >6 cm → **toxic megacolon**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dysregulated mucosal immune response to intestinal microbiota in genetically susceptible hosts

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stool **C. difficile** testing and cultures before attributing worsening diarrhea to inflammation
Fecal calprotectin supports intestinal inflammation; **ileocolonoscopy with biopsies** confirms
Suspected small-bowel disease or abscess → CT/MR enterography; avoid capsule with suspected stricture
Partial SBO, suspected stricture → enterography; older exam questions may expect **water-soluble small-bowel follow-through**
Fulminant colitis → abdominal radiograph and limited sigmoidoscopy; avoid full colonoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute severe UC → hospitalization, **IV methylprednisolone**, fluids, VTE prophylaxis
Steroid-refractory severe UC → infliximab or cyclosporine; perforation or megacolon → urgent colectomy
★ Moderate/severe flare without obstruction or abscess → **prednisone** induces remission only; **never maintenance**
Crohn abscess → antibiotics and drainage before immunosuppression
UC with colorectal cancer → **total proctocolectomy**, not segmental colectomy

rows.label: Complications
items: Fistulas (enterovaginal → vaginal flatus), strictures, obstruction in Crohn; colectomy does not cure Crohn
Terminal ileal Crohn → B12 deficiency, **bile salt malabsorption** → steatorrhea
Colonic disease → colorectal cancer; active inflammation → venous thromboembolism

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Colonic disease → surveillance colonoscopy beginning about **8 years** after onset; PSC → immediately
Vaccinate and screen TB/HBV before biologics; smoking cessation for Crohn

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS: no bleeding, weight loss or inflammatory markers
Ischemic colitis: abrupt pain followed by hematochezia, vascular risk

table.title: Distribution and outpatient treatment
rows: RLQ mass, cobblestones, perianal disease, granulomas
Bloody diarrhea, tenesmus; friability, crypt abscesses, pseudopolyps

informed-consent-and-capacity.name: Informed consent and capacity
informed-consent-and-capacity.scope: Decision-making capacity, informed consent, emergency exception (implied consent), refusal of treatment, AMA discharge
informed-consent-and-capacity.core: A capable adult may accept or refuse treatment after understanding its benefits, material risks, alternatives, and consequences of refusal.

rows.label: Principle
items: ★ Capacity: **understand, appreciate (own case), reason, communicate**; decision-specific, fluctuating
Competence: legal; diagnosis, age, alcohol use, incarceration, disagreement alone ≠ incapacity

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Explain benefits, material risks, alternatives/no treatment; **qualified interpreter and teach-back**
Correct delirium, intoxication, pain, communication barriers; reassess capacity
AMA request: assess capacity, explore barriers, offer safer plan, document discussion and follow-up

rows.label: Don't
items: Capable refusal → respect choice, even if life-saving or pregnant; avoid coercion, abandonment
No valid consent → possible **battery**; signed form alone insufficient
Refusing one therapy (blood) ≠ refusing all; provide other indicated care, including surgery

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ Emergency + incapacity + no surrogate/directive/verified refusal → implied consent to treat
★ Parents refuse minor's life-saving transfusion → **treat emergency**; seek court authority if feasible
Incapacity without emergency → authorized surrogate; involve patient to remaining ability

rows.label: Traps
items: Psychiatric illness does not automatically remove capacity; assess the specific decision
Suicide danger may justify protective detention despite expressed desire to leave
New material procedure or changed risk → renewed consent; consent revocable anytime before procedure

table.title: Who decides
rows: Ask whom to involve; facilitate promptly; no override
Minor decides; no parental consent (state law varies)
Parents seek unproven remedy for child
Continue proven therapy; investigate remedy; CPS not first
Close; discuss after waking; no next-of-kin consent
Autonomy ≠ entitlement; physician refuses, explains, offers alternatives

informed-consent-and-capacity.evidence: Not checked online; established consent/capacity ethics; emergency and minor-consent law varies by jurisdiction.

inherited-bleeding-disorders.name: Inherited bleeding disorders
inherited-bleeding-disorders.scope: Hemophilia A, Hemophilia B, von Willebrand disease, factor XI deficiency, hemarthrosis, mixing studies, factor VIII inhibitors
inherited-bleeding-disorders.core: Deep tissue bleeding suggests a coagulation-factor defect; mucosal bleeding suggests platelet/von Willebrand dysfunction, even with a normal platelet count.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hemophilia A/B: X-linked, usually males; maternal family history may be absent
vWD usually autosomal dominant; factor XI deficiency autosomal, enriched in Ashkenazi ancestry

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Recurrent **hemarthroses**, muscle hematomas and delayed postoperative bleeding → hemophilia
Epistaxis, gingival bleeding, easy bruising and heavy menses → vWD
Factor XI deficiency: variable postsurgical bleeding, especially oral/urologic procedures; hemarthrosis uncommon
Unexpected major bleeding after circumcision or surgery may reveal previously undiagnosed disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: VIII/IX/XI deficits impair intrinsic-pathway thrombin generation and fibrin stabilization
vWF mediates platelet adhesion and stabilizes factor VIII; deficiency impairs primary and sometimes secondary hemostasis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ CBC/platelets, PT, aPTT; **mixing study corrects** factor deficiency, fails with inhibitor
Factor VIII, IX or XI activity identifies deficiency; hemophilia generally normal PT/platelets
★ Suspected vWD → **vWF antigen, activity and factor VIII**; aPTT may be normal
Stress, pregnancy and estrogen raise vWF; repeat borderline testing when clinically stable
Severe hemophilia: factor activity <1%; inhibitor testing if replacement response is inadequate

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Major suspected hemophilic bleeding → **replace deficient factor immediately**, before imaging delays
Hemophilia A → factor VIII; B → factor IX; emicizumab prophylaxis for selected A
Mild responsive A or type 1 vWD → **desmopressin after response testing**
Severe vWD → vWF-containing concentrate; avoid desmopressin in type 2B and ineffective type 3
Mucosal bleeding → tranexamic acid; factor XI procedures → antifibrinolytic ± plasma with hematology planning

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic hemarthropathy, intracranial hemorrhage, anemia; factor inhibitors complicate replacement
Desmopressin → water retention/hyponatremia; factor concentrates can increase thrombosis risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Individualized factor/nonfactor prophylaxis, dental care, procedure planning; avoid aspirin and nonselective NSAIDs
Family genetic counseling; fluid restriction and sodium monitoring around desmopressin

rows.label: Mimics
items: ITP: low platelets with mucocutaneous bleeding
Acquired factor VIII inhibitor: new bleeding, mixing fails to correct
Vitamin K deficiency: PT prolonged first

intracranial-hemorrhage.name: Intracranial hemorrhage
intracranial-hemorrhage.scope: Intracerebral hemorrhage, hypertensive hemorrhage, amyloid angiopathy, coagulopathy reversal, blood pressure management
intracranial-hemorrhage.core: Acute focal neurologic deficits with headache, vomiting, or depressed consciousness require immediate CT to identify intraparenchymal bleeding and guide reversal.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Chronic hypertension, older age, anticoagulants/coagulopathy, stimulant use
Vascular malformation, tumor, venous thrombosis; lobar recurrence in older adults suggests cerebral amyloid angiopathy

rows.label: Clues
items: Rapid progression, seizure, severe BP elevation; small bleeds may resemble ischemic stroke
★ Hypertensive sites: **putamen, thalamus, pons, cerebellum**; amyloid favors superficial lobar locations
Declining consciousness, asymmetric pupils, abnormal posturing → mass effect/herniation
Cerebellar injury: vomiting, severe ataxia, vertigo; rapid deterioration possible despite initially preserved alertness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Small-artery lipohyalinosis or amyloid deposition weakens vessel walls
Expanding hematoma, intraventricular extension, and perihematomal edema cause secondary injury

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Noncontrast head CT now**; CBC/platelets, INR/PTT, renal function, glucose, medication history
CTA/vascular imaging for younger patients, atypical location, suspected malformation; repeat CT for deterioration/expansion
MRI susceptibility imaging identifies microbleeds and underlying lesions after stabilization
Do not give thrombolysis or perform LP for established parenchymal hemorrhage

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Airway, head elevation, neuro-ICU; **stop anticoagulants and reverse immediately**
★ Mild/moderate ICH, SBP 150–220 → IV **nicardipine/clevidipine**, target ~140, maintain 130–150 mm Hg
Large/severe ICH requires individualized perfusion goals; avoid abrupt excessive BP reduction or SBP <130
Cerebellar deterioration, hydrocephalus, brainstem compression, or volume ≥15 mL → **urgent surgical evacuation**
Hydrocephalus → ventricular drain; herniation → hypertonic saline/mannitol; treat seizures, no routine prophylaxis

rows.label: Complications
items: Hematoma expansion, hydrocephalus, herniation, seizures, disability, recurrent hemorrhage
★ **No routine platelet transfusion** for antiplatelet-associated ICH without emergency surgery/severe thrombocytopenia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Long-term BP control, smoking/stimulant cessation; reassess anticoagulation using recurrence and embolic risks
Intermittent pneumatic compression immediately; low-dose heparin prophylaxis after bleeding stability is documented

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ischemic stroke: no acute blood on CT; SAH: thunderclap, sulcal/cisternal blood
Hemorrhagic tumor: mass/edema pattern, enhancement; confirm with MRI

learning-disorders.name: Learning disorders
learning-disorders.scope: Specific learning disorder with impairment in reading (dyslexia), written expression (dysgraphia), mathematics (dyscalculia), individualized education plan (IEP)
learning-disorders.core: Persistent difficulty acquiring specific academic skills despite targeted instruction, with impairment exceeding that explained by intellectual, sensory, or educational factors.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, prematurity, developmental language disorder
ADHD frequently coexists; bilingualism or socioeconomic disadvantage alone does not establish a disorder

rows.label: Clues
items: Academic difficulty disproportionate to functioning in other domains; frustration, avoidance, low confidence
Onset during school years; deficits may emerge only when demands exceed compensatory strategies
★ Reading difficulty reflects phonologic processing, **not simply reversing letters**
Persistent effort without expected skill acquisition distinguishes disability from occasional poor performance

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Neurodevelopmental differences in domain-specific information processing; unrelated to laziness
Skills improve with intervention, but underlying vulnerability often persists into adulthood

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Difficulties **≥6 months despite targeted support** + substantially below-age academic achievement
Individual standardized achievement testing + developmental, educational, and psychosocial history
★ Assess **hearing and vision**; evaluate language, attention, attendance, and quality of instruction
IQ–achievement discrepancy not required; global cognitive/adaptive deficits suggest intellectual disability instead
Evaluate each affected domain; multiple impairment specifiers may apply

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ School evaluation → **IEP** with explicit specialized instruction, measurable goals, periodic progress review
Reading: systematic phonics/phonemic-awareness instruction; writing/math: structured domain-specific teaching
Accommodations: extended time, assistive technology, reduced distraction; 504 plan when access accommodations suffice
Treat comorbid ADHD when present; stimulants do not directly remediate academic skill deficits

rows.label: Complications
items: School avoidance, dropout, anxiety/depression, reduced self-esteem
Unrecognized difficulties may be mislabeled as defiance or poor motivation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early developmental/literacy surveillance and prompt intervention reduce secondary academic and emotional harm
Coordinate family, school, and clinicians; reinforce strengths and protect against bullying

rows.label: Mimics
items: Intellectual disability: broad intellectual and adaptive impairments
ADHD: pervasive inattention across settings; skill deficits may coexist
Inadequate schooling: insufficient instruction or limited language exposure explains performance

table.title: Academic domains
rows: Spelling, grammar, organization of written ideas

learning-disorders.evidence: Not checked against a current guideline online; established DSM-based educational and pediatric teaching.

low-back-pain.name: Low back pain
low-back-pain.scope: Lumbosacral strain, herniated disk and radiculopathy, spinal stenosis, red flags, imaging indications, conservative management
low-back-pain.core: Most acute low back pain improves with activity and analgesia; neurologic deficits or systemic red flags change the workup.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heavy lifting, deconditioning, obesity, prolonged sitting
Cancer, immunosuppression, injection drug use, osteoporosis, chronic glucocorticoids increase serious-pathology risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Mechanical pain varies with movement; isolated axial pain without systemic illness favors benign disease
★ **Urinary retention, saddle anesthesia, bilateral weakness** → cauda equina emergency
Fever, weight loss, night pain, trauma, or progressive weakness → targeted urgent evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Paraspinal injury causes localized pain; degenerative narrowing or disk extrusion compresses neural structures

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ No red flags → **no initial imaging**, including routine radiographs
Focused strength, reflex, sensory, gait examination; straight-leg raise supports lower lumbar radiculopathy
★ Suspected infection, malignancy, cord compression → **MRI**; suspected fracture → radiograph or CT
Persistent symptoms despite about 6 weeks' care → MRI if intervention being considered
Suspected spinal infection → ESR/CRP, blood cultures; normal temperature does not exclude infection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Continue activity**, no heavy lifting until pain resolves, heat, short NSAID course; avoid prolonged bed rest
Physical therapy if pain persists despite NSAIDs; avoid routine opioids and systemic steroids
Progressive motor deficit or cauda equina → urgent surgical decompression
Refractory disabling radicular pain → epidural injection or diskectomy after imaging correlation

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic pain, functional limitation, medication dependence
Untreated compression → permanent bladder, bowel, sexual, or motor dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: Core strengthening, regular exercise, ergonomic lifting, weight management

rows.label: Mimics
items: AAA: abdominal pulsatile mass, vascular risk, hypotension
Renal colic: flank-to-groin pain, hematuria; inflammatory back pain: improves with exercise
Vascular claudication: calf pain, bicycling too; standing still relieves; weak pulses alone don't exclude stenosis

table.title: Mechanical patterns
rows: Leg pain below knee; cough aggravates
Shopping-cart sign; pulses usually preserved; MRI confirms

low-back-pain.evidence: Not checked online; established generalist back-pain evaluation.

lyme-disease.name: Lyme disease
lyme-disease.scope: Borrelia burgdorferi, erythema migrans, early localized, early disseminated, late Lyme arthritis, doxycycline, ceftriaxone
lyme-disease.core: Ixodes-transmitted Borrelia infection progresses from an expanding skin lesion to neurologic, cardiac, or joint disease when untreated.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Wooded/brush exposure in Northeast, mid-Atlantic, upper Midwest; attached blacklegged tick
Tick exposure may be unnoticed; small-mammal reservoirs sustain transmission

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Erythema migrans**: enlarging lesion >5 cm, days after bite; central clearing not required
Early dissemination: multiple lesions, unilateral/**bilateral facial palsy**, lymphocytic meningitis, fluctuating AV block
Late disease: intermittent large-joint swelling, especially knee; severe pain less prominent than effusion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Spirochete inoculation → local multiplication, hematogenous spread, inflammatory injury
Persistent antibodies can remain after cure and do not prove viable infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical erythema migrans → **clinical diagnosis**, no serology needed
Other compatible disease → two-tier serology: EIA followed by immunoblot or second EIA
Early localized serology may be negative; isolated IgM after >30 days is unreliable
Joint-fluid PCR supports selected arthritis cases; CSF testing for CNS disease; ECG for cardiac symptoms

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized skin disease → **doxycycline 10 days**, or amoxicillin/cefuroxime 14 days
Facial palsy/mild neurologic disease may use oral doxycycline; severe CNS disease → IV ceftriaxone
★ Symptomatic carditis, PR ≥300 ms, higher-degree block → **hospitalize, telemetry, IV ceftriaxone**; pacing if needed
Lyme arthritis → 28-day oral course; persistent objective disease requires reassessment, sometimes IV ceftriaxone
Post-treatment nonspecific fatigue → supportive evaluation; no prolonged antibiotics without objective reinfection/failure

rows.label: Complications
items: Complete heart block, meningoencephalitis, recurrent arthritis, postinfectious joint inflammation
Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction shortly after antibiotics; not necessarily drug allergy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ High-risk Ixodes bite, attachment ≥36 hours, endemic region → **single-dose doxycycline within 72 hours of removal**
Tick checks, permethrin-treated clothing, DEET; remove tick with fine tweezers near skin
No prophylaxis for low-risk bite or routine serologic testing of asymptomatic patients

rows.label: Mimics
items: Immediate bite hypersensitivity: small, itchy, does not progressively enlarge
Septic arthritis: marked pain, toxicity, positive culture; babesiosis: hemolysis and intraerythrocytic parasites
Neurosyphilis: Lyme can falsely react on syphilis serology; tick exposure + facial palsy → Borrelia antibodies

macrocytic-anemia.name: Macrocytic anemia
macrocytic-anemia.scope: Folate deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, pernicious anemia, hypersegmented neutrophils, methylmalonic acid and homocysteine
macrocytic-anemia.core: MCV >100 fL prompts separation of megaloblastic DNA-synthesis failure from alcohol, liver disease, hypothyroidism, reticulocytosis, and marrow disorders.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Vegan diet without supplementation, gastric bypass, ileal disease/resection, metformin, long-term **PPI** → B12 depletion
Alcohol misuse, poor intake, pregnancy, methotrexate, trimethoprim → folate depletion; stores last months, B12 years
Autoimmune gastritis → pernicious anemia; nitrous oxide functionally inactivates cobalamin

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, glossitis; ineffective erythropoiesis may raise LDH/indirect bilirubin and lower other cell lines
★ **Paresthesias, gait ataxia, impaired vibration/proprioception** → B12 deficiency, even without anemia
Smooth macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils indicate megaloblastic change

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Defective thymidine synthesis delays nuclear maturation relative to cytoplasm
B12-dependent myelin metabolism explains spinal cord/peripheral nerve injury; folate deficiency lacks this syndrome
B12 malabsorption corrected by oral intrinsic factor → **gastric IF loss** (atrophic gastritis), not ileal disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC, smear, reticulocytes, B12**; assess folate, liver tests, TSH, exposures
Borderline B12 → methylmalonic acid; renal impairment can elevate it independently
★ Suspected pernicious anemia → **anti-intrinsic-factor antibodies**; highly specific but not fully sensitive
High reticulocytes → bleeding/hemolysis; unexplained cytopenias/dysplasia → bone marrow evaluation for MDS
Coexisting iron deficiency may normalize MCV; neurologic suspicion still requires B12 evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Replace B12 before or with folate**; folate alone can conceal ongoing neurologic injury
Neurologic/severe deficiency or malabsorption → parenteral B12 initially; irreversible cause requires lifelong replacement
Dietary B12 deficiency may respond to high-dose oral replacement; folate deficiency → oral folic acid
Remove causative drug/exposure where possible; monitor reticulocyte response and count recovery

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated B12 deficiency → irreversible neurologic disability; severe disease → pancytopenia
Pernicious anemia → increased gastric adenocarcinoma and neuroendocrine tumor risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Reliable B12 supplementation for vegans**; lifelong monitoring/replacement after relevant GI surgery
Folic acid before conception and early pregnancy; improve nutrition and reduce harmful alcohol intake

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcohol-associated macrocytosis: round macrocytes, no required megaloblastic change
Myelodysplasia: persistent multilineage cytopenia, dysplastic marrow
Reticulocytosis: polychromasia after blood loss or hemolysis

macrocytic-anemia.evidence: Not checked online; established hematology and nutritional teaching.

macular-degeneration.name: Macular degeneration
macular-degeneration.scope: Dry age-related macular degeneration (drusen), wet age-related macular degeneration (neovascularization), metamorphopsia, Amsler grid, anti-VEGF
macular-degeneration.core: Older adult with painless central visual loss, preserved peripheral vision, and straight lines appearing wavy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, cigarette smoking, family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Reading and face recognition difficulty; central scotoma in advanced disease
★ Rapid decline over days to weeks → urgent assessment for wet conversion

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dry: degeneration of retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptors
Wet: VEGF-mediated choroidal neovascularization beneath the macula

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Dilated macular exam** and OCT; fluorescein angiography if neovascular diagnosis uncertain
★ Home **Amsler grid**: cover one eye at a time; fixate center with reading correction

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Wet: serial intravitreal **anti-VEGF** such as aflibercept or ranibizumab, guided by OCT
Selected geographic atrophy → intravitreal pegcetacoplan or avacincaptad pegol to slow expansion
Low-vision rehabilitation and magnification for persistent reading or daily activity impairment

rows.label: Complications
items: Permanent central vision loss from geographic atrophy or disciform scar
Pain and rapidly worsening acuity after intravitreal injection → suspect endophthalmitis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **AREDS2** for intermediate AMD or advanced AMD in one eye; no benefit in early AMD
Stop smoking; avoid beta-carotene formulations in current or former smokers

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cataract: diffuse blur, glare and lens opacity
Retinal detachment: flashes, floaters, peripheral curtain

macular-degeneration.evidence: Checked AAO Age-Related Macular Degeneration Preferred Practice Pattern (2026 update).

measures-of-association.name: Measures of association
measures-of-association.scope: Relative risk (RR), odds ratio (OR), attributable risk (AR), absolute risk reduction (ARR), number needed to treat (NNT), number needed to harm (NNH), hazard ratio
measures-of-association.core: Relative measures describe proportional associations; absolute measures incorporate baseline risk and determine treatment benefit or harm.

rows.label: Definition
items: CER = control event rate; EER = experimental event rate
Two-by-two table: exposed events/non-events a/b; unexposed events/non-events c/d
Relative risk reduction (RRR; vaccine efficacy) = (CER − EER)/CER = 1 − RR

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ Ratio null = **1**; risk-difference null = **0**
★ Hazard ratio compares instantaneous event rates over time; not cumulative risk ratio
NNT/NNH require specified outcome and follow-up duration; always round up

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ RR: cohort/RCT; OR: case-control and logistic regression
Attributable risk: excess incidence among exposed attributable to exposure, assuming causality
HR: survival analysis with censoring; constant interpretation assumes proportional hazards

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Use proportions, not percentage numbers, in reciprocal calculations
OR approximates RR only with rare outcomes; common outcomes exaggerate relative association
Association alone cannot establish causality; confounding can distort every measure

measures-of-association.evidence: Statistical definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

medical-errors-and-patient-safety.name: Medical errors and patient safety
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.scope: Near miss, adverse event, error disclosure, root cause analysis, structured sign-outs and handoffs
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.core: Protect the patient first, disclose errors honestly, and redesign systems to reduce recurrence.

rows.label: Principle
items: Just culture: distinguish human error, risky shortcuts, and reckless conduct
